entries.title: TSCF header mandatory usage for presentation-time requests
entries.summary: The TSCF header version 0 shall be used for RCP requests that are to be executed no earlier than the presentation time included in the header.
entries.citation: p.23, "as it shall be used for RCP requests which shall be executed earliest at the included presentation time"

entries.title: TSCF-Header Version 0 layout
entries.summary: Bit-field layout diagram of the Time-Synchronous Control Format (TSCF) header, version 0, used to precede RCP requests carrying a presentation time.
entries.citation: p.23, Figure 5 caption: "TSCF-Header Version 0"

entries.title: NTSCF header mandatory usage for immediate/conditional requests
entries.summary: The NTSCF header version 0 shall be used for RCP requests executed as soon as possible or under request-specific conditions, and for all responses and acknowledges.
entries.citation: p.23, "The corresponding NTSCF header in version 0 shall be used for RCP requests which shall be executed as soon as possible or under request specific conditions as well as for responses and acknowledge."

entries.title: NTSCF-Header Version 0 layout
entries.summary: Bit-field layout diagram of the Non-Time-Synchronous Control Format (NTSCF) header, version 0, used for immediate/conditional requests, responses, and acknowledges.
entries.citation: p.23, Figure 6 caption: "NTSCF-Header Version 0"

entries.title: Drop behavior for TSCF AVTPDUs when time-sync unsupported
entries.summary: When time-synchronization is not supported by the receiving endpoint/RC Server, an AVTPDU carrying a TSCF header is dropped and no response is sent.
entries.citation: p.23, "In case time-synchronization is not supported, AVTPDUs having a TSCF header are dropped, and no response send."

entries.title: TSCF-received requests execute no earlier than presentation time
entries.summary: For any of the three basic request types (standard, conditional, cancel), if the request is received under a TSCF header it shall be executed no earlier than the presentation time given in that header.
entries.citation: p.24, "If received under TSCF header all of them shall be executed earliest at the given presentation time."

entries.title: Conditional-request execution gating
entries.summary: For conditional requests (compound, compound wait, trigger-based, chained, timed), the specified condition needs to come true before execution of the request may start.
entries.citation: p.24, "The condition needs to come true before the execution starts"

entries.title: Cancel-request removal capability
entries.summary: A cancel request can be used to remove requests that are pending execution from an endpoint's request storage.
entries.citation: p.24, "Requests that are pending for execution can be removed from endpoint request storage by this type of request."

entries.title: ACF_ABB used for standard and timed requests
entries.summary: The RC Client uses the ACF_ABB message format for standard requests and for timed requests sent under a TSCF header.
entries.citation: p.24, "The RC Client uses ACF_ABB format for standard requests and timed requests (under TSCF header)"

entries.title: ACF_GBB with mtv=0 for conditional requests
entries.summary: The RC Client uses ACF_GBB format for conditional requests, encoding the condition in the message_time_stamp field; the mtv (message-timestamp-valid) bit is cleared to 0 to signal this alternative use of those bytes.
entries.citation: p.24, "The RC Client uses ACF_GBB format for conditional requests... The message_timestamp valid bit is cleared (mtv=0) to indicate this alternative usage of the bytes."

entries.title: ACF_GBB with mtv=0 for cancel requests
entries.summary: The RC Client uses ACF_GBB format for cancel requests, encoding the cancel condition in the message_time_stamp field; the mtv bit is cleared to 0 to signal this alternative use of those bytes.
entries.citation: p.24, "The RC Client uses ACF_GBB format for cancel requests... The message_timestamp valid bit is cleared (mtv=0) to indicate this alternative usage of the bytes."

entries.title: Standard request support is mandatory
entries.summary: Support for the standard request type (unconditional execution) is a mandatory feature of RCP endpoints.
entries.citation: p.25, section heading "11.2.1 Standard request – unconditional execution of request (mandatory feature)"

entries.title: Standard request shall use ACF_ABB format
entries.summary: A best-effort standard request shall be sent using the ACF_ABB message format.
entries.citation: p.25, "A request that is meant for best effort execution shall be sent in ACF_ABB format."

entries.title: Standard request postponed under TSCF header
entries.summary: If a standard request is received under a TSCF header, its execution is postponed until the presentation time given in that header has occurred.
entries.citation: p.25, "If received under TSCF header, the execution of this request is postponed until the presentation time has occurred."

entries.title: ABB message standard request layout
entries.summary: Bit/byte-field layout diagram of an ACF_ABB message used for a standard request, showing the byte message info fields (acf_msg_type, acf_msg_length, pad, mtv, rsv, byte_bus_id, evt, hs, cs, transaction_num, op, rsp, err, ms, read_size/segment_num) and the byte_msg_payload.
entries.citation: p.25, Figure 7 caption: "ABB message standard request"

entries.title: ABB message field definitions for standard requests
entries.summary: Defines each field of the ACF_ABB standard-request message: acf_msg_type=0x0E, acf_msg_length (quadlet count of GBB-style payload), pad (padding octets), mtv=0b, rsv=00b, byte_bus_id (endpoint identifier), evt (endpoint-specific, see section 13.5), hs=0b, cs=0b, transaction_num, op (0b=response-with-data expected, 1b=not expected), rsp=0b (marks message as request), err=0b, ms (0b=fragment sequence complete, 1b=more ABB messages follow), and read_size/segment_num (read_size if op=0, else segment_num).
entries.citation: p.25, Table 4 caption: "Usage of ABB message for standard requests"

entries.title: Safety-request retention on MSB-set condition identifiers
entries.summary: For Compound, Compound wait and Trigger conditional requests, if the MSB of the first message_timestamp byte (identifier 0x8x) is set, the request is treated as a safety request and shall not be deleted when the EP needs to enter safe state.
entries.citation: p.26, "If the MSB of the identifier (0x8x) is set the request is treated as a safety request and will not be deleted when the EP needs to go to safe state."

entries.title: Conditional request type identifiers
entries.summary: Defines the first-byte values of message_timestamp that identify each conditional-request subtype: 0x0F/0x8F Compound, 0x0B/0x8B Compound wait, 0x0E/0x8E Triggered, 0x01 Chained, 0x0A Timed. Marked with an editorial note that it is pending update pending acceptance of the new trigger-request proposal.
entries.citation: p.26, Table 5: "Different types of conditional requests"

entries.title: Unsupported trigger-request handling
entries.summary: Handling trigger requests is optional for an RC Server; if not supported, the RC Server shall drop received trigger requests and send a response with the err-bit set and error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD.
entries.citation: p.27, "In case this is not supported, trigger requests shall be dropped, and a response send with err-bit set and error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD."

entries.title: Endpoint-generated HW trigger events
entries.summary: Each endpoint may generate one or more hardware trigger events, each described individually in that endpoint's own chapter.
entries.citation: p.27, "Each endpoint may generate one or more HW trigger events."

entries.title: Execution-based trigger event generation
entries.summary: Each request may generate an execution-based trigger event at the end of its own execution, in addition to any HW trigger events the endpoint generates.
entries.citation: p.27, "Each request may also generate an execution based trigger event at the end of its execution."

entries.title: GBB message layout and field semantics for trigger requests
entries.summary: Defines the ACF_GBB byte-message layout for trigger requests (request_type, trigger_source_ep, trigger_signal_nr, trigger_threshold, trigger_exec_delay, trigger_repetitions, pos_trigger_out, neg_trigger_out and standard evt/hs/cs/transaction_num/op/rsp/err/ms fields). The field explanation states request_type is 0x0F or 0x8F for a trigger request — this conflicts with Table 5 (p.26), which assigns 0x0F/0x8F to "Compound" and reserves 0x0E/0x8E for "Triggered"; the Compare request in §11.2.2.4 (p.33) instead uses 0x0E/0x8E, matching Table 5's "Triggered" codes, suggesting Table 6's request_type value here is a stale/inconsistent leftover from before the harmonization proposal.
entries.citation: p.27-28, Table 6: "Usage of GBB message for trigger requests"; field row (p.27) "request_type ... 0x0F or 0x8F for trigger request"

entries.title: Unsupported compound-request handling
entries.summary: Handling compound requests is optional for an RC Server; if not supported, the RC Server shall drop received compound requests and send a response with the err-bit set and error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD.
entries.citation: p.29, "In case this is not supported, compound requests shall be dropped, and a response send with err-bit set and error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD."

entries.title: cmp_start_state=0 wildcard-state execution
entries.summary: If cmp_start_state is 0, the compound request shall be started regardless of the sequencer's current state, unless the sequencer is disabled, in which case execution is prohibited.
entries.citation: p.29, "If cmp_start_state = 0 then the request shall be started in any state unless the sequencer is disabled which will prohibit the execution of the compound request."

entries.title: Ordering guidance for repetitive wildcard-state compound requests
entries.summary: A repetitive compound request with cmp_start_state=0 should either be the last compound request sent to an EP or include cmp_exec_delay much greater than 0, otherwise it will hinder execution of other compound requests and lower-priority requests.
entries.citation: p.29, "Such compound request, if repetitive, should either be the last compound request sent to an EP or include a cmp_exec_delay >>0, since otherwise this will hinder execution of other compound requests and further requests with lower priority."

entries.title: GBB message byte layout for compound requests
entries.summary: Byte-layout diagram of the ACF_GBB message used for compound requests, showing acf_msg_type/length/pad/mtv/rsv/byte_bus_id, request_type=compound, cmp_start_state, cmp_next_state, cmp_sequencer, cmp_exec_delay, cmp_repetitions and the evt/hs/cs/transaction_num/op/rsp/err/ms/read_size fields.
entries.citation: p.29, Figure 8: "GBB message for compound requests"

entries.title: Compound request_type value
entries.summary: The request_type field of a compound request shall be encoded as 0x0F (non-safety) or 0x8F (safety).
entries.citation: p.29, "The request_type field for a compound request shall be 0x0F or 0x8F."

entries.title: Compound-request watchdog-overflow queue behavior
entries.summary: On a watch-dog overflow configured to trigger safe state and a safety operation, compound requests coded 0x0F shall be cleared from the queue while those coded 0x8F remain active, since 0x8F requests belong to the safety sequence executed on watch-dog triggering.
entries.citation: p.29, "compound requests with 0x0F will be cleared from the queue while the requests with 0x8F remain active after watch-dog overflow as they belong to the safety sequence to be executed based on the watch-dog triggering."

entries.title: Field explanations for compound-request GBB message
entries.summary: Defines the semantics of each field in the compound-request GBB message: cmp_start_state, cmp_next_state, cmp_sequencer, cmp_exec_delay (in multiples of ep_delay_time [1µs,20µs,20µs,50µs]), cmp_repetitions (including 0xFFFF = infinite repetition, 0 = single execution), plus evt/hs/cs/transaction_num/op/rsp/err/ms/read_size-segment_num.
entries.citation: p.30, Table 7: "Usage of GBB message for compound requests"

entries.title: Unsupported compound-wait-request handling
entries.summary: Handling compound wait requests is optional for an RC Server; if not supported, the RC Server shall drop received compound wait requests and send a response with the err-bit set and error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD.
entries.citation: p.31, "In case this is not supported, compound wait requests shall be dropped, and a response send with err-bit set and error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD."

entries.title: Compound-wait condition-met response timing
entries.summary: When the wait condition is found met, the cmpw_exec_delay must expire before a response is generated; if the condition is not met, request execution is finalized with no further action.
entries.citation: p.31, "When the check finds that the condition is met the cmpw_exec_delay needs to expire before a response is generated, else the request execution is finalized without further action."

entries.title: cmpw_start_state=0 wildcard-state execution
entries.summary: If cmpw_start_state is 0, the compound wait request shall be started regardless of the sequencer's current state, unless the sequencer is disabled, in which case execution is prohibited.
entries.citation: p.31, "If cmpw_start_state = 0 then the request shall be started in any state unless the sequencer is disabled which will prohibit the execution of the compound wait request."

entries.title: Ordering guidance for repetitive wildcard-state compound-wait requests
entries.summary: A repetitive compound wait request with cmpw_start_state=0 should either be the last compound request sent to an EP or include cmpw_exec_delay much greater than 0, to avoid hindering execution of other compound requests and lower-priority requests when EP output state changes frequently.
entries.citation: p.31, "Such compound wait request, if repetitive, should either be the last compound request sent to an EP or include a cmpw_exec_delay >>0, since otherwise this might hinder execution of other compound requests and further requests with lower priority when the EP output state changes frequently."

entries.title: GBB message byte layout for compound wait requests
entries.summary: Byte-layout diagram of the ACF_GBB message used for compound wait requests, showing request_type=compound wait, cmpw_start_state, cmpw_next_state, cmpw_sequencer, cmpw_exec_delay, cmpw_repetitions and the evt/hs/cs/transaction_num/op/rsp/err/ms/read_size fields.
entries.citation: p.31, Figure 9: "GBB message for compound wait requests"

entries.title: Compound-wait request_type value
entries.summary: The request_type field of a compound wait request shall be encoded as 0x0B (non-safety) or 0x8B (safety), consistent with Table 5's Compound-wait identifiers.
entries.citation: p.31, "The request_type field for a compound wait request shall be 0x0B or 0x8B."

entries.title: Compound-wait watchdog-overflow retention behavior
entries.summary: On a watch-dog overflow of the stream that registered the request, compound wait requests coded 0x0B shall be cleared while those coded 0x8B remain active.
entries.citation: p.31, "Compound wait requests with 0x0B will be cleared in case of a watch-dog overflow of the stream that registered this request, while those with 0x8B remain active after watch-dog overflow."

entries.title: cs-bit execution-due semantics for compound wait
entries.summary: The cs bit determines when a compound wait request becomes due for execution: cs=0 means due once the sequencer reaches cmpw_start_state; cs=1 means due only after the EP output state has changed following the sequencer reaching cmpw_start_state (useful when updates are driven by triggered operations rather than sequencer state, to ensure the condition is checked against recent data).
entries.citation: p.31, "If cs = 0, then compound wait request is due for execution, when the sequencer is in the cmpw_start_state. If cs = 1, then compound wait request is due for execution, when EP output state has changed after the sequencer reached the cmpw_start_state."

entries.title: Field explanations for compound-wait-request GBB message
entries.summary: Defines the semantics of each field in the compound-wait-request GBB message: cmpw_start_state, cmpw_next_state, cmpw_sequencer, cmpw_exec_delay (multiples of ep_delay_time), cmpw_repetitions (0xFFFF = infinite, 0 = single execution), cs (0b = check condition immediately when request started, 1b = check after next EP output state update), plus evt/hs/transaction_num/op/rsp/err/ms/read_size-segment_num.
entries.citation: p.32, Table 8: "Usage of GBB message for compound wait requests"

entries.title: Unsupported compare-request handling
entries.summary: Handling compare requests is optional for an RC Server; if not supported, the RC Server shall drop received compare requests and send a response with the err-bit set and error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD.
entries.citation: p.33, "In case this is not supported, compare requests shall be dropped, and a response send with err-bit set and error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD."

entries.title: Endpoint-generated HW trigger events (compare-request context)
entries.summary: Each endpoint may generate one or more hardware trigger events, described per endpoint chapter. This sentence duplicates §11.2.2.1's text verbatim, appearing to be a copy-paste holdover in the draft rather than content specific to compare requests.
entries.citation: p.33, "Each endpoint may generate one or more HW trigger events."

entries.title: Execution-based trigger event generation (compare-request context)
entries.summary: Each request may generate an execution-based trigger event at the end of its execution. This sentence duplicates §11.2.2.1's text (with a typo "am execution based" for "an execution based"), again appearing to be copy-paste boilerplate rather than compare-request-specific content.
entries.citation: p.33, "Each request may also generate an execution based trigger event at the end of its execution."

entries.title: GBB message byte layout for compare requests
entries.summary: Byte-layout diagram of the ACF_GBB message used for compare requests, showing request_type=triggered compare, trigger_source_ep, trigger_signal_nr, trigger_threshold, a wait field, trigger_repetitions, pos_trigger_out, neg_trigger_out and the standard evt/hs/cs/transaction_num/op/rsp/err/ms/read_size fields. The compare request generates a trigger event based on comparing byte_msg_payload against interface data or register content, with evt-bits controlling the comparison condition (e.g. '>' or '<'). Note: the field-explanation table for this figure continues past page 33 (out of this slice's page range) and is not cataloged here.
entries.citation: p.33, Figure 10: "GBB message for compare requests"

entries.title: Compare-request GBB field usage (Table 9, cont.)
entries.summary: Continuation of Table 9 defining GBB message field usage for compare (conditional) requests: pos_trigger_out/neg_trigger_out generate a trigger_event_nr (bits[7:6]=10b, bits[5:0]=pos/neg_trigger_out) on true/false compare result respectively, plus standard byte-message-info field values (evt, hs=0b, cs=0b, transaction_num, op, rsp=0b, err=0b, ms, read_size/segment_num).

entries.title: Unsupported triggered requests dropped
entries.summary: Handling triggered requests is an optional RC Server function; if unsupported, the RC Server shall drop triggered requests and send a response with the err-bit set and error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD.
entries.citation: p.35, §11.2.2.5: 'In case this is not supported, triggered requests shall be dropped, and a response send with err-bit set and error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD.'

entries.title: Endpoint trigger-signal generation
entries.summary: Each endpoint may generate one or more trigger signals, described separately per endpoint type.
entries.citation: p.35: 'Each endpoint may generate one or more trigger signals.'

entries.title: Endpoint configurable to start on trigger
entries.summary: Each endpoint may be configured to start a request upon receiving a selected trigger signal.
entries.citation: p.35: 'Each endpoint may be configured to start a request upon receiving a selected trigger signal.'

entries.title: GBB message layout for triggered requests
entries.summary: Wire-format diagram (Figure 11) of the ACF_GBB request for triggered requests, showing request_type=triggered plus trigger_source_ep, trigger_signal_nr, trigger_threshold, trigger_exec_delay, and trigger_repetitions fields alongside the standard byte_message_info fields.
entries.citation: p.35, 'Figure 11 – GBB message for triggered requests'

entries.title: Triggered request_type values and watchdog persistence
entries.summary: The request_type field of a triggered request shall be 0x0E or 0x8E; 0x0E-type requests are cleared on a stream watch-dog overflow, while 0x8E-type requests remain active across watch-dog overflow.
entries.citation: p.35-36: 'The request_type field for a triggered request shall be 0x0E or 0x8E. Triggered requests with 0x0E will be cleared in case of a watch-dog overflow of the stream that registered this request, while those with 0x8E remain active after watch-dog overflow.'

entries.title: Triggered-request GBB field usage (Table 10)
entries.summary: Defines byte-message-info field usage for triggered-request GBB messages: trigger_source_ep (source endpoint of the trigger), trigger_signal_nr, trigger_threshold (number of trigger occurrences before execution, 0-based), trigger_exec_delay (delay in multiples of EP's ep_delay_time after threshold reached), trigger_repetitions (repeat count, 0xFFFF=infinite, 0=single execution, decremented and request removed from EP storage at zero), plus evt/hs=0b/cs=0b/transaction_num/op/rsp=0b/err=0b/ms/read_size-segment_num.
entries.citation: p.35-36, Table 10 caption: 'Table 10: Usage of GBB message for triggered requests'

entries.title: Unsupported chained requests dropped
entries.summary: Handling chained requests is an optional RC Server function; if unsupported, the RC Server shall drop chained requests and send a response with err-bit set and error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD.
entries.citation: p.37, §11.2.2.6: 'In case this is not supported, chained requests shall be dropped, and a response send with err-bit set and error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD.'

entries.title: Forced-sequential execution via chaining
entries.summary: When a single AVTPDU contains more than one request, their execution can be forced to be sequential by using the chained request type; a chain may start at any request in the AVTPDU except the last, of any request type.
entries.citation: p.37: 'the execution of the requests can be forced to be sequential by using chained requests. A chain can start with any (except the last) request in an AVTPDU...'

entries.title: ACF_GBB layout for chained requests
entries.summary: Wire-format diagram (Figure 12) of the ACF_GBB chained-request message, showing request_type=chained, chain_exec_delay, two reserved fields, and the standard byte_message_info fields including cs (conditional start).
entries.citation: p.37, 'Figure 12 - ACF_GBB for chained requests'

entries.title: Chain waits on predecessor completion
entries.summary: Two or more chained requests execute such that each request always waits for its predecessor request to finish execution before starting; e.g., if the first request has a WAIT condition, the whole chain only starts after that condition becomes true.
entries.citation: p.37: 'the second and following requests always wait on the predecessor request to finish its execution.'

entries.title: First-request-in-chain restriction and CHAIN_ERROR
entries.summary: A chain request cannot be the first request in an AVTPDU (there is no predecessor); if it is, the entire chain is ignored and each affected EP generates an error response with error code CHAIN_ERROR, unless suppressed by EP configuration.
entries.citation: p.37: 'If the first request in an AVTPDU is a chain request, then there is no predecessor to chain to, thus the entire chain will be ignored. An error response with the error code "CHAIN_ERROR" to each request will be generated by the respective EPs, if not suppressed by EP configuration.'

entries.title: Chain cannot span multiple AVTPDUs
entries.summary: A chain of requests cannot span over multiple AVTPDUs; all chained requests must be contained within a single AVTPDU.
entries.citation: p.37: 'A chain of requests cannot span over multiple AVTPDUs.'

entries.title: Chain repetition follows first command's count
entries.summary: If the first request in a chain has a repetition count greater than zero, the entire chain is repeated in execution according to that first command's repetition count.
entries.citation: p.37: 'If the first request in a chain has a repetition count > 0, then the whole chain will be repeated in execution based on the first command's repetition count.'

entries.title: Chain removal from EP storage at repetition exhaustion
entries.summary: When no further repetitions of a chained request are to be executed, the request shall be removed from the EP request storage.
entries.citation: p.37: 'When no further repetitions are to be executed, then the request shall be removed from the EP request storage.'

entries.title: No duplicate start of unfinished chained request
entries.summary: If a chained request has not finalized its execution (e.g., still waiting for exec_delay to expire) when its predecessor finalizes execution again, the chained request is not started a second time.
entries.citation: p.37: 'In case a chained request hasn't finalized its execution (e.g. still waiting for the exec_delay to expire) when the predecessor finalizes execution again, then the chained request is not started a second time.'

entries.title: Chained-request GBB field usage (Table 11)
entries.summary: Defines byte-message-info field usage for chained-request GBB messages: request_type=0x01, two reserved fields that shall be written 0 (else request rejected), chain_exec_delay (delay in multiples of ep_delay_time after predecessor finalizes), cs = Conditional start bit, plus standard evt/hs=0b/transaction_num/op/rsp=0b/err=0b/ms/read_size-segment_num fields.
entries.citation: p.38, Table 11 caption: 'Table 11: Usage of GBB message for chained requests'

entries.title: Conditional-start (cs) bit semantics for chained requests
entries.summary: The cs bit governs conditional chain continuation: cs=0b executes the request even if the previous request in the chain returned an error; cs=1b skips execution (and the remainder of the chain) if the previous request errored, sending an error response with error code CHAIN_ABORTED, and if the chain is repetitive it restarts from the beginning.
entries.citation: p.38: 'cs Conditional start 0b: request will be executed even in case the previous request returned an error 1b: request will not be executed in case the previous request returned an error... error response with error code = CHAIN_ABORTED. In case the chain is repetitive as per initial request it starts over.'

entries.title: Timed request via TSCF avtp_timestamp
entries.summary: A request that must execute at a predefined point in time can be sent under a TSCF header, with the avtp_timestamp field serving as the presentation time.
entries.citation: p.39: 'requests can be sent under TSCF header, where an avtp_timestamp is included, that servs as a presentation time.'

entries.title: Timed-request GBB layout (original, 48-bit presentation_time)
entries.summary: Wire-format diagram (Figure 13) of the timed-request ACF_GBB message: request_type=0x0A (timed), a reserved field, and a 48-bit presentation_time split as presentation_time[47:32] in byte_message_info and presentation_time[31:0], alongside the standard byte_message_info fields.
entries.citation: p.39, 'Figure 13 – Timed request'

entries.title: Timed-request GBB layout (0.5.1_RC3 proposal, with trigger outputs)
entries.summary: Alternate/updated ACF_GBB timed-request layout (introduced as an 0.5.1_RC3 proposal, embedded in the RC5 body text) that truncates presentation_time to 44 bits (split [43:20]/[19:0], yielding a shorter ~4-hour rollover vs. the original 48-bit/~3.25-day rollover) and adds pos_trigger_out and neg_trigger_out fields to generate trigger events.
entries.citation: p.39: 'Proposal in 0.5.1_RC3: Updated format that allows to generate trigger events'; field text p.39-40: 'presentation_time = (AS_sec × 10^9 + AS_ns) mod 2^48 ... (thus rolls over every 3,25 days / 4 hours in case of the updated proposal)'

entries.title: Timed-request GBB field usage (Table 12)
entries.summary: Defines byte-message-info field usage for timed-request GBB messages: request_type=0x0A, reserved field that shall be written 0 (else rejected), presentation_time computed as (AS_sec×10^9 + AS_ns) mod 2^48 (gPTP-derived), plus standard evt/hs/cs/transaction_num/op/rsp/err/ms/read_size-segment_num fields.
entries.citation: p.39-40, Table 12 caption: 'Table 12: Usage of GBB message for timed request'

entries.title: hs/cs bits reserved-zero for timed requests
entries.summary: For timed requests, the hs and cs bits shall be written as 0; otherwise the request shall be rejected with error code UNSUPPORTED_CMD.
entries.citation: p.40, Table 12: 'hs, cs All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD'

entries.title: TSCF presentation_time precedence over avtp_timestamp
entries.summary: When a timed request is received under a TSCF header, the presentation_time carried in the request itself shall prevail; the TSCF header's avtp_timestamp is ignored.
entries.citation: p.41: 'In case a timed request is received under TSCF header the presentation_time in the request shall prevail, the avtp_timestamp of the TSCF header is ignored.'

entries.title: presentation_time as earliest execution point
entries.summary: In any case, the presentation_time value denotes the earliest point in time at which the timed request shall be executed.
entries.citation: p.41: 'In any case the presentation_time is the earliest point in time, when the request shall be executed.'

entries.title: Rejection of far-future timed requests
entries.summary: The RC Server may reject a timed request when its presentation_time is too far in the future (threshold is implementation-dependent), returning error code PRESENTATION_TIME_TOO_FAR.
entries.citation: p.41: 'The RC Server may reject the request, when the presentation_time is too far in the future, which is implementation dependent (error code = PRESENTATION_TIME_TOO_FAR).'

entries.title: Timed request rejection when gPTP unsynchronized
entries.summary: If time synchronization has not been established, timed requests (whether in the native ACF_GBB format or under a TSCF header) shall be rejected and an error response shall be sent with error code GPTP_FAIL.
entries.citation: p.41: 'In case the time synchronization hasn't been established, timed requests (either in the format shown here or under TSCF header) shall be rejected and an error response shall be sent (error code = GPTP_FAIL).'

entries.title: Sync loss must not affect request execution
entries.summary: If gPTP synchronization is lost, the local time continues based on the local oscillator and may become imprecise; this imprecision shall not have an impact on request execution (the RC Server continues executing timed requests against its local time).
entries.citation: p.41: 'the local time continues based on the available local oscillator, which might lead to an imprecise representation of the time. This shall not have an impact of request execution.'

entries.title: RC Client duty to cancel imprecise-time requests
entries.summary: It is the RC Client's responsibility to actively cancel timed requests it no longer wants executed when the local representation of time is not precise (e.g., after synchronization loss), since the RC Server will not withhold execution on that basis.
entries.citation: p.41: 'It is the RC Client's duty to cancel requests in case they shall not be executed when the local representation of time is not precise.'

entries.title: Cancellable window excludes requests under execution
entries.summary: A request can be cancelled while pending or after being started but only until it is under execution; requests already under execution will not be aborted by a cancellation.
entries.citation: p.42, "A request can be cancelled while it is pending and after it has been started until it is under execution. Requests under execution will not be aborted."

entries.title: Chained successor cancellation propagation
entries.summary: If a request that has other requests chained to it is cancelled, the RC Server shall also cancel the chained successor requests.
entries.citation: p.42, "If a request is cancelled to which a request is chained, then the chained successors shall be cancelled by the RC Server as well."

entries.title: Cancelled request generates REQUEST_CANCELED error response
entries.summary: Every request that is cancelled results in an error response being sent with error code = REQUEST_CANCELED.
entries.citation: p.42, "Each request that is cancelled will send an error response with the error code = REQUEST_CANCELED."

entries.title: Clear-all-requests mandatory cancellation option
entries.summary: Mandatory cancellation option that clears all requests received in the same stream as the cancellation request from an EP request storage; identified by request_type = 0x05 (first byte of the message_timestamp field), with evt, hs and cs fields required to be zero.
entries.citation: p.42, "the request type (first byte in the message_timestamp field) is 0x05. Evt, hs and cs shall be zero."

entries.title: Figure 14 - Clear-all-requests GBB message layout
entries.summary: ACF_GBB byte layout for the mandatory clear-all-requests cancellation message: acf_msg_type=0x0D, request_type=0x05, evt/hs/cs, transaction_num, op/rsp/err/ms, read_size/segment_num, with byte_msg_payload carrying CRC only when the EP is in safe mode (else omitted).
entries.citation: p.42, Figure 14 caption: "Request cancellation of all requests in EP request queue"

entries.title: RC3-proposal trigger-generating clear-all-requests format (status ambiguous in RC5)
entries.summary: An alternate GBB byte layout for the clear-all-requests message, labeled "Proposal in 0.5.1_RC3", replacing part of the reserved field with pos_trigger_out/neg_trigger_out fields to allow trigger-event generation; it retains an unresolved editorial comment marker (Commented [BE13]) and has no assigned figure number, so whether it is confirmed normative content of RC5 (vs. leftover unmerged proposal text) should be verified before implementations rely on it.
entries.citation: p.42, "Proposal in 0.5.1_RC3: Updated format that allows to generate trigger events:" (annotation "Commented [BE13]: 0.5.1RC3: trigger generation added")

entries.title: Table 13 - GBB field usage to cancel all requests
entries.summary: Field-by-field definition of the request_type=0x05 GBB cancellation message: acf_msg_type=0x0D, reserved bits shall all be 0 else the request is rejected, evt encoding (0000b none / 1000b ack-on-file), hs=0, cs=0, transaction_num, op/rsp/err/ms semantics, and read_size/segment_num.
entries.citation: p.42-43, Table 13 caption: "Usage of GBB message to cancel all requests"

entries.title: Clear-all-non-safestate-requests optional cancellation feature
entries.summary: Optional cancellation feature clearing only the non-safestate requests received in the same stream as the cancellation request from an EP request storage; identified by request_type = 0x06, with evt, hs and cs fields required to be zero when implemented.
entries.citation: p.43, "11.2.3.2 Clear all non-safestate requests (optional feature)" ... "the request type (first byte in the message_timestamp field) is 0x06. evt, hs and cs shall be zero."

entries.title: Figure 15 - Clear-all-non-safestate-requests GBB message layout
entries.summary: ACF_GBB byte layout for the optional clear-all-non-safestate-requests cancellation message (request_type=0x06), structured identically to Figure 14's field layout.
entries.citation: p.43, Figure 15 caption: "Request cancellation of all non-safestate requests in EP request queue"

entries.title: RC3-proposal trigger-generating clear-non-safestate format (status ambiguous in RC5)
entries.summary: An alternate GBB byte layout for the clear-all-non-safestate-requests message, labeled "Proposal in 0.5.1_RC3", adding pos_trigger_out/neg_trigger_out fields; carries an unresolved editorial comment marker (Commented [BE14]) and no figure number, so its normative status in RC5 should be verified.
entries.citation: p.43, "Proposal in 0.5.1_RC3: Updated format that allows to generate trigger events:" (annotation "Commented [BE14]: 0.5.1RC3: trigger generation added")

entries.title: Table 14 - GBB field usage to clear all non-safestate requests
entries.summary: Field-by-field definition of the request_type=0x06 GBB cancellation message; notably states evt[2:0], hs, and cs bits shall all be written as 0 else the request shall be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD.
entries.citation: p.43-44, Table 14 caption: "Usage of GBB message to clear all all non-safestate requests" (evt[2:0], hs, cs row: "All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD")

entries.title: Clear-one-single-request optional cancellation feature
entries.summary: Optional cancellation feature that clears exactly one queued request identified by clear_transaction_num, scoped to the stream and byte_bus_id in which it was originally received (transaction_num is only unique within that scope); identified by request_type = 0x07 followed by the transaction_num to cancel, with evt, hs and cs required to be zero.
entries.citation: p.45, "11.2.3.3 Clear one single request (optional feature)" ... "Mind that the transaction_num is only unique in the context of the stream and byte_bus_id with that it has been received."

entries.title: Figure 16 - Cancel-single-request GBB message layout
entries.summary: ACF_GBB byte layout for cancelling a single specific request (request_type=0x07), including the clear_transaction_num field in place of the reserved byte_bus_id-adjacent field used by Figures 14/15.
entries.citation: p.45, Figure 16 caption: "Cancellation of a single, specific request"

entries.title: RC3-proposal trigger-generating single-request-cancel format (status ambiguous in RC5)
entries.summary: An alternate GBB byte layout for the single-request cancellation message, labeled "Proposal in 0.5.1_RC3", adding pos_trigger_out/neg_trigger_out fields; carries an unresolved editorial comment marker (Commented [BE15]) and no figure number, so its normative status in RC5 should be verified.
entries.citation: p.45, "Proposal in 0.5.1_RC3: Updated format that allows to generate trigger events:" (annotation "Commented [BE15]: 0.5.1RC3: trigger generation added")

entries.title: Table 15 - GBB field usage to cancel a single, specific request
entries.summary: Field-by-field definition of the request_type=0x07 GBB cancellation message, including clear_transaction_num (transaction_num of the request in this stream to be cancelled), reserved bits shall be 0 else request rejected, evt/hs/cs, transaction_num, op/rsp/err/ms, and read_size/segment_num.
entries.citation: p.45-46, Table 15 caption: "Usage of GBB message to cancel a single, specific request"

entries.title: Single-cancel outcome: REQUEST_NOT_FOUND vs. no-payload success
entries.summary: If the clear_transaction_num referenced by a single-request cancellation is not found, the cancellation generates an error response with error code = REQUEST_NOT_FOUND; otherwise a response without byte_msg_payload is sent to report success.
entries.citation: p.46, "The request initiating the cancellation will create an error response with the error code = REQUEST_NOT_FOUND, when the clear_transaction_num was not found. Else a response without byte_msg_payload will be sent to report success."

entries.title: Table 16 - Taxonomy of RCP response types
entries.summary: Defines the four RCP-specific response types layered over IEEE1722's single generic response concept: Acknowledge (request accepted for execution), Write Response (successful write execution), Read Response (successful read execution, includes data), and Error Response (non-successful execution).
entries.citation: p.47, Table 16 caption: "Types of responses"

entries.title: Response ACF format selected by timestamp presence
entries.summary: Responses that include a timestamp are carried in ACF_GBB format; responses without a timestamp are carried in ACF_ABB format.
entries.citation: p.47, "In case responses include a timestamp, they are in ACF_GBB format, else in ACF_ABB format."

entries.title: Table 17 - ABB/GBB message field usage for responses
entries.summary: Field-by-field definition of the ABB/GBB response message: acf_msg_type (0x0E ABB no timestamp / 0x0D GBB with message_timestamp), mtv validity meaning, evt[3:0] encoding (0x0 simple/data/error response, 0x1-0x8 response counter with rollover from 0x8 to 0x1, 0x9-0xE reserved, 0xF acknowledge), transaction_num and op mirrored from the originating request, rsp=1, err flag, ms fragmentation flag, and read_size/segment_num.
entries.citation: p.47, Table 17 caption: "Usage of ABB/GBB message for responses"

entries.title: Acknowledge response identified by evt=0xF, no payload
entries.summary: A response with evt[3:0] = 0xF is an acknowledge and never carries a byte_msg_payload.
entries.citation: p.48, "With evt[3:0] = 0xF the response is an acknowledge. It does not contain a byte_msg_payload."

entries.title: Acknowledge err-field semantics (filed vs. rejected)
entries.summary: Within an acknowledge, err=0 confirms the request has been filed into an EP request storage with no byte_msg_payload; err=1 indicates the request has been rejected and the byte_msg_payload contains an error code.
entries.citation: p.48, "err = 0 confirms that the request has been filed into an EP request storage. No byte_msg_payload in this case. err = 1 indicates that the request has been rejected. The byte_msg_payload contains an error code."

entries.title: Write Response identification and no-payload rule
entries.summary: A response with evt[3:0] < 0x9 and op = 1 is a write response confirming successful execution of a write request, and it carries no byte_msg_payload.
entries.citation: p.48, "With evt[3:0] < 0x9 and op = 1 the response is a write response and confirms successful execution of a write request. It does not have a byte_msg_payload."

entries.title: Read Response identification and payload rule
entries.summary: A response with evt[3:0] < 0x9 and op = 0 is a read response confirming successful execution of a read request, and it carries a byte_msg_payload whose content depends on the type and configuration of the sending endpoint.
entries.citation: p.48, "With evt[3:0] < 0x9 and op = 0 the response is a read response and confirms successful execution of a read request. It has a byte_msg_payload which depends on the type and the configuration of the endpoint sending this response."

entries.title: Error Response identification and payload rule
entries.summary: A response with evt[3:0] < 0x9 and err = 1 is an error response indicating request execution failure, and it carries a byte_msg_payload containing an error code.
entries.citation: p.48, "With evt[3:0] < 0x9 and err = 1 the response is an error-response indicating that the execution of the request failed. It has a byte_msg_payload which contains an error code."

entries.title: Optional RC Server clock synchronization via gPTP
entries.summary: An RC Server may synchronize an internal clock to a system clock (using IEEE802.1AS/gPTP) to support time-synchronous execution of requests and timestamping of responses and acknowledges.
entries.citation: p.49, "An RC Server may synchronize an internal clock to a system clock to support time synchronous execution of requests within an RC System as well as timestamping of responses and acknowledge. This can be done using IEEE802.1AS (gPTP)."

entries.title: RC Server clock is a receiving clock
entries.summary: The RC Server's internal clock is defined as a receiving (slave) clock, not a grandmaster/source clock, in the gPTP hierarchy.
entries.citation: p.49, "The RC Server clock is a receiving clock."

entries.title: avtp_timestamp computation for TSCF header (32-bit, 4s rollover)
entries.summary: For a version-0 TSCF header, avtp_timestamp = (AS_sec x 10^9 + AS_ns) mod 2^32, computed from the gPTP seconds and nanoseconds fields, and rolls over every 4 seconds.
entries.citation: p.49, "avtp_timestamp = (AS_sec × 10^9 + AS_ns) mod 2^32 where AS_sec is the gPTP seconds field and AS_ns is the gPTP nanoseconds field (thus rolls over every 4 seconds)"

entries.title: message_timestamp computation for ACF_GBB capture timestamps (64-bit, ~585yr rollover)
entries.summary: For capture timestamps in ACF_GBB response and acknowledge messages, message_timestamp = (AS_sec x 10^9 + AS_ns) mod 2^64, computed from the gPTP seconds and nanoseconds fields, and rolls over every 584.9 years.
entries.citation: p.49, "message_timestamp = (AS_sec × 10^9 + AS_ns) mod 2^64 where AS_sec is the gPTP seconds field and AS_ns is the gPTP nanoseconds field (thus rolls over every 584,9 years)"

entries.title: ACF_GBB timestamp field represents capture time
entries.summary: Timestamps carried in ACF_GBB messages sent by the RC Server represent the time at which information was captured, held in the message_timestamp field.
entries.citation: p.49, "Time stamps in the ACF_GBB type sent by the RC Server represent the time when information has been captured and are in message_timestamp field."

entries.title: Per-endpoint independent timestamp-creation selection
entries.summary: Whether timestamps are created can be independently selected per endpoint, separately for response messages and for acknowledge messages.
entries.citation: p.49, "Whether time stamps shall be created, can be selected for responses and acknowledge separately individually per endpoint."

entries.title: Default to ACF_ABB (no timestamp) when timestamping unrequested
entries.summary: When timestamping was not requested for an endpoint, the RC Server shall use the ACF_ABB format without a timestamp as the default for any data it transmits.
entries.citation: p.49, "When timestamping was not requested, then the ACF_ABB type format without time stamp shall be default for any data transmitted by the RC Server."

entries.title: Acknowledge timestamp = time of acceptance into EP request storage
entries.summary: The timestamp carried by an acknowledge represents the point in time when the request was accepted by the respective EP request storage for execution.
entries.citation: p.49, "The timestamp of an acknowledge represents the point in time when the request has been accepted by the respective EP request storage for execution."

entries.title: Response timestamp = time input signal captured at physical interface
entries.summary: The timestamp carried by a response represents the point in time when an input signal was captured at the physical interface; per-endpoint-type details are given in the respective endpoint sections.
entries.citation: p.49, "The timestamp of a response represents the point in time when an input signal has been captured at the physical interface."

entries.title: Optional TSCF header processing carrying presentation timestamp
entries.summary: A presentation timestamp (avtp_timestamp) can appear in the TSCF header and applies to all requests carried under that header; processing of TSCF headers by the receiving RC Server is an optional feature.
entries.citation: p.49, "A presentation time stamp (avtp_timestamp) can be found in the TSCF header and is valid for all requests under this header. Processing of TSCF headers is optional."

entries.title: Presentation timestamp defines earliest execution time
entries.summary: A presentation timestamp denotes the earliest point in time at which the message shall be executed by the addressed endpoint(s).
entries.citation: p.49, "Presentation time stamps are the earliest point in time, when a message shall be executed by the addressed endpoint(s)."

entries.title: RC Server may reject requests with far-future presentation time
entries.summary: The RC Server may reject a request when its presentation time is too far in the future; the threshold for "too far" is implementation-dependent.
entries.citation: p.49, "The RC Server may reject the request, when the presentation time is too far in the future, which is implementation dependent."

entries.title: TSCF/NTSCF header usage split between RC Client and RC Server
entries.summary: TSCF headers are sent only by RC Clients and never by RC Servers; the RC Server always uses the NTSCF header and conveys capture timestamps solely via message_timestamp in ACF_GBB.
entries.citation: p.49, "TSCF headers will only be sent by RC Clients, never by the RC Servers. The RC Server always uses NTSCF header and only uses message_timestamp in ACF_GBB to convey a capture timestamp."

entries.title: RC Server request handling to Endpoints
entries.summary: The RC Server shall handle requests from one or multiple RC Clients addressed to its Endpoints; responses and acknowledges received from the Endpoints are handled by the RC Responder.
entries.citation: p.50, "The RC Server shall handle requests from one or multiple RC Client(s) which are addressed to its Endpoints."

entries.title: RC Server config access provision
entries.summary: The RC Server shall provide access to its own configuration and the configuration of all its Endpoints, as well as the RC Responder; configuration is stored locally in the RC Server's configuration memory as a list of parameters.
entries.citation: p.50, "The RC Server shall provide access to its own configuration and the configuration of all its Endpoints, as well as the RC Responder."

entries.title: RC Server status/debug access provision
entries.summary: The RC Server shall provide access to status and debug information from its Endpoints and itself.
entries.citation: p.50, "The RC Server shall provide access to status and debug information from its Endpoints and itself."

entries.title: Mandatory RC Server implementation features
entries.summary: Every TC18-compliant RC Server shall support: NTSCF header processing; standard request handling; implementation of Endpoint 0; and a cancellation request to clear all requests from an EP request storage (see 11.2.3.1).
entries.citation: p.50, "There are a few mandatory features that each TC18 compliant RC Server shall support: NTSCF header processing - Standard request handling - Implementation of Endpoint 0 - Cancellation request to clear all requests from an EP request storage"

entries.title: Optional time-synchronization bundle
entries.summary: An RC Server may optionally support a time-synchronization bundle comprising TSCF header processing, gPTP (IEEE802.1as) implementation, timed request support (see 11.2.2.7), and time-stamped acknowledges/responses.
entries.citation: p.50, "Optional support for time-synchronization comes as a bundle of: - TSCF header processing - Implementation of gPTP (IEEE802.1as) - Support of timed request ... - Time stamped acknowledges - Time stamped responses"

entries.title: Optional enhanced request cancellation
entries.summary: An RC Server may optionally support enhanced request cancellation, i.e. clearing a single request from an EP request storage (see 11.2.3.3).
entries.citation: p.50, "Optional support for enhanced request cancellation includes: - Clear one single request from an EP request storage (see 11.2.3.3)"

entries.title: Optional compound requests bundle
entries.summary: An RC Server may optionally support compound requests as a bundle: request types 0x0F/0x8F (see 11.2.2.2) and 0x0B/0x8B (see 11.2.2.3), implementation of at least four sequencers (see 12.10), and a clear-all-non-safestate-requests operation on an EP request storage (see 11.2.3.2).
entries.citation: p.50, "Optional support of compound requests comes as bundle of - Support of compound requests (request types 0x0F and 0x8F) ... - Implementation of at least four sequencers (see 12.10) - Clear all non-safestate requests from an EP request storage"

entries.title: Start-up lifecycle state
entries.summary: After a power cycle or restart, the RC Server shall start in the lifecycle state it is actually configured in (via NVM-persisted state or, absent NVM, default settings that may place it in an advanced state).
entries.citation: p.51, "the RC Server shall start in the life-cycle state it is actually configured in"

entries.title: RC Server lifecycle states diagram
entries.summary: Figure 17 depicts the RC Server lifecycle state machine across HW_UNCONFIGURED, HW_CONFIGURED, and RCP_CONFIGURED, including discovery-stream assignment, state-transition triggers (root client / discovery stream / stream-bb_id access), and error responses DISCOVERY_STREAM_OCCUPIED, HW_CFG_INCONSISTENT, LOCKED_CONFIG_ACCESS, and EPs_NOT_IDLE.
entries.citation: p.51, Figure caption: "Figure 17 - RC Server lifecycle states"

entries.title: Configuration only via discovery stream
entries.summary: In HW_UNCONFIGURED, all configuration requests must be run via the stream that was used for discovery.
entries.citation: p.52, "All configurations must be run via the stream which was used for discovery."

entries.title: NTSCF-only acceptance in HW_UNCONFIGURED
entries.summary: In HW_UNCONFIGURED state only AVTPDUs having an NTSCF header are accepted; all others are dropped without further response.
entries.citation: p.52, "In this state only AVTPDUs having a NTSCF header are accepted and all others are dropped without further response."

entries.title: ACF_ABB-to-EP0-only requests in HW_UNCONFIGURED
entries.summary: Within the discovery stream, only ACF_ABB configuration requests are supported and must be directed to EP0 via byte_bus_id 0x00; all other requests are dropped without further response.
entries.citation: p.52, "Within the stream only requests ACF_ABB are supported for configuration, and all requests need to be directed to EP0 via the discovery byte_bus_id 0x00. All other requests are dropped without further response."

entries.title: EP0 full register-map access in HW_UNCONFIGURED
entries.summary: Via EP0 the entire register map (i.e. all endpoints) can be accessed for both read and write in HW_UNCONFIGURED state.
entries.citation: p.52, "Via EP0 the entire register map (i.e. all endpoints) can be accessed (read and write access)."

entries.title: Unicast-only write requests (HW_UNCONFIGURED)
entries.summary: Write requests shall only be accepted when sent in unicast frames while in HW_UNCONFIGURED state.
entries.citation: p.52, "Write requests shall only be accepted when sent in unicast frames."

entries.title: HW_UNCONFIGURED to HW_CONFIGURED transition rules
entries.summary: A write to svr_lifecycle_state can advance the state to HW_CONFIGURED; a request to advance directly to RCP_CONFIGURED will be rejected with an error response.
entries.citation: p.52, "A request to advance the state directly to RCP_CONFIGURED will be rejected with an error response."

entries.title: HW_CONFIGURED plausibility check
entries.summary: Advancement to HW_CONFIGURED requires a plausibility check that all EPs configured for use (ep_used=1) match the HW_config pin mapping and have a request-queue configuration; if implausible, the request is rejected with error HW_CFG_INCONSITENT.
entries.citation: p.52, "If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with HW_CFG_INCONSITENT."

entries.title: HW config locked in HW_CONFIGURED
entries.summary: In HW_CONFIGURED state, access to the RC Server's HW configuration shall have been concluded, and all access to HW_config and EP_generic_config is locked.
entries.citation: p.52, "access to the HW configuration of the RC Server shall have been concluded and as such all access to the HW_config and EP_generic_config are locked"

entries.title: Frame/header filtering and unicast writes (HW_CONFIGURED)
entries.summary: In HW_CONFIGURED state, AVTPDUs with a TSCF header and requests in ACF_GBB format are dropped without further response; write requests shall only be accepted when sent in unicast frames.
entries.citation: p.52, "AVTPDUs having a TSCF header are dropped without further response, as well as requests in ACF_GBB format. Write requests shall only be accepted when sent in unicast frames."

entries.title: Per-EP functional configuration accessibility
entries.summary: The functional configuration of each individual EP shall be accessible for read and write as described in 12.7.1, via requests using the stream_id and byte_bus_id assigned to that EP by configuration (see 12.7.8).
entries.citation: p.52, "The functional configuration of each individual EP shall be accessible for read and write as described in 12.7.1"

entries.title: Restricted EP0 write access to other EPs (HW_CONFIGURED)
entries.summary: Write access via EP0 to other EPs' configuration is only possible for a configured root client or via the discovery stream; non-config requests to EPs other than EP0 will be ignored and dropped without response.
entries.citation: p.52, "Write access via EP0 to other EPs configuration is only possible for a configured “root client” of via the discovery stream. Request to EPs other than EP0 that are not config requests will be ignored and dropped without response."

entries.title: HW_CONFIGURED to RCP_CONFIGURED transition rules
entries.summary: A write to svr_lifecycle_state can advance the state to RCP_CONFIGURED; the request must come via the discovery stream or a valid stream_id/byte_bus_id combination, restricted to the root client's combination if a root client is configured.
entries.citation: p.52, "The request needs to come either via the discovery stream or via a valid stream_id/byte_bus_id combination. If a root client is configured only the root clients stream_id/byte_bus_id is accepted besides the discovery stream."

entries.title: RCP_CONFIGURED plausibility check
entries.summary: Advancement to RCP_CONFIGURED requires a plausibility check that each used EP has at least one stream_id/byte_bus_id association, each configured stream has at least one stream_id/byte_bus_id, and each configured response stream is assigned to at least one request stream; if implausible, the request is rejected with error RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT.
entries.citation: p.52, "If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT"

entries.title: Reverting to HW_UNCONFIGURED
entries.summary: The lifecycle state can be reverted from HW_CONFIGURED to HW_UNCONFIGURED via a write to svr_lifecycle_state, sent within the discovery stream or a valid stream_id/byte_bus_id combination (restricted to the root client's combination if configured).
entries.citation: p.52, "it is also possible to go back to state HW_UNCONFIGURED via a write request to the server functional configuration entry svr_lifecycle_state"

entries.title: Write access locked in RCP_CONFIGURED
entries.summary: In RCP_CONFIGURED state, all configuration has been finished so all write access to configuration spaces is locked except write access to EPs' functional configurations, allowed via their dedicated stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations or via root client EP0 access.
entries.citation: p.52, "all write access to configuration spaces is locked and only write access to the EP’s functional configurations is allowed via their dedicated stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations or via root client access EP0"

entries.title: EP enable gates operational request execution
entries.summary: While an EP is not enabled (ep_enable), it will only execute config requests; operational requests are stored in the EP's queue and execution starts once the EP is enabled, with an acknowledge sent after storing if requested.
entries.citation: p.53, "as long as EPs are not enabled (ep_enable in the EP functional config) they will only execute config requests. Operational requests will be stored in the EP’s queue and execution started when EP is enabled."

entries.title: Unicast-only config writes (RCP_CONFIGURED)
entries.summary: Configuration write requests shall only be accepted when sent in unicast frames in RCP_CONFIGURED state.
entries.citation: p.53, "Configuration write requests shall only be accepted when sent in unicast frames."

entries.title: Restricted EP0 access to other EPs (RCP_CONFIGURED)
entries.summary: Access via EP0 to other EPs' configuration is only possible via the root client's stream, if a root client is configured.
entries.citation: p.53, "Access via EP0 to other EPs configuration is only possible by the root clients stream, if configured."

entries.title: R/W column notation semantics
entries.summary: Write access to some parameters may be prohibited depending on lifecycle state, denoted in tables' R/W column by W* (write prohibited depending on lifecycle state) versus W (write access possible anytime).
entries.citation: p.53, "this is marked by * in the R/W-column of the respective tables (W*: write prohibited in depending on lifecycle state. W: write access possible anytime)"

entries.title: Persistent client-side discovery cache
entries.summary: During the RCP Framework's discovery state, the RC Client can permanently store all discovered RC Servers and their properties, and can later act on a-priori-known discovery information without re-running discovery.
entries.citation: p.54, "The RC Client can permanently store all discovered RC Servers and their properties."

entries.title: Optional power modes and mode definitions
entries.summary: The RC Server may support different power modes: Unpowered (no sufficient power), Powered (sufficient power for all functions, subject to lifecycle state), Sleep (lowest power, woken by dedicated WakePin or network interface), and StandBy (lowest power while keeping configuration data and functional wake-up sources alive).
entries.citation: p.55, "The RC Server may support different power modes."

entries.title: Power and operation modes diagram
entries.summary: Figure 18 depicts the RC Server power/operation mode state machine covering Unpowered, Powered, Sleep, and StandBy modes and their transitions.
entries.citation: p.55, Figure caption: "Figure 18 – power and operation modes"

entries.title: Cold-start lifecycle state
entries.summary: After a cold start (power-on or wake from Sleep) the RC Server shall be in its configured lifecycle state, with the actual state readable from svr_lifecycle_state; configuration may derive from device defaults or NVM restore.
entries.citation: p.55, "After a cold start the RC Server will be in its configured lifecycle state. ... The actual state after cold start will be readable from svr_lifecycle_state."

entries.title: Configuration maintained across hot-start
entries.summary: In a hot-start (wake-up from StandBy), the configuration does not need to be redone, as it shall be maintained during low-power mode.
entries.citation: p.55, "In hot-start the configuration does not need to be redone, as it shall be maintained during low-power mode."

entries.title: Hot-start wake-up procedure (internal EP/wakepin source)
entries.summary: On wake-up via an internal EP signal or dedicated wakepin, the RC Server first enables the network interface and checks availability, initiating a network WakeUp if unavailable; once the network is available it repeatedly sends a WakeUp response (with wake-up source) on the responder stream configured for the original standby request until a valid AVTPDU is received from the sleep-request Client, with the repetition time configurable in the WakeUp EP; upon valid reception, all used endpoints and response queues are enabled (potentially re-enabling heartbeat response streams).
entries.citation: p.55, "the RC Server will send via the responder stream which is configured for the original standby request a repetitive response to the sleep request with a WakeUp message and the WakeUp source. The message will be repeated until a valid AVTPDU from the sleep request Client is received."

entries.title: TC14/TC10 network wake-up source handling
entries.summary: If the wake-up source is a TC14/TC10 wake-up request on the network, this also wakes the RC Server, which directly checks network availability and proceeds with the same procedure as the internal-source case.
entries.citation: p.55, "If the wake-up source was a TC14/TC10 wake-up request on the network this will also wake the RC Server, but it will directly check for the network availability and proceed as before."

entries.title: StandBy/Sleep initiation channels
entries.summary: StandBy can only be initiated via a request to the RC Server; Sleep can be initiated either via a valid TC14/TC10 sleep request on the network or via a request to the RC Server, and only an RC Client allowed to access the RC Server endpoint can request entry into standby or sleep mode.
entries.citation: p.56, "StandBy can only be initiated via request to the RC Server"

entries.title: StandBy mode power behavior
entries.summary: In standby mode the power consumption shall be reduced and only the wake-up control shall be active.
entries.citation: p.56, "In standby mode the power consumption shall be reduced and only the wake-up control shall be active."

entries.title: Sleep mode power behavior
entries.summary: In sleep mode the power consumption shall be reduced to a bare minimum and only part of the network PHY shall be powered (e.g. PMIC switched off via INH, PHY runs on VBAT).
entries.citation: p.56, "In sleep mode the power consumption shall be reduced to a bare minimum and only part of the network PHY shall be powered."

entries.title: Wake-up event aborts sleep entry
entries.summary: If a wake-up-source event defined in the wake-up endpoint occurs during processing of the sleep request, the request is not executed and the RC Server does not enter sleep mode.
entries.citation: p.56, "If an event defined as wake-up source in the wake-up endpoint occurs during the processing of the sleep-request, the request is not executed, and the RC Server does not enter sleep mode."

entries.title: Sleep/standby rejection conditions
entries.summary: The RC Server shall reject a sleep/standby request with error REQUEST_CANCELED when the wake-up event register (wup_status) is not cleared, at least one EP is not idle, or a responder queue has a message pending for transmission.
entries.citation: p.56, "The RC Server will reject requests to enter sleep or standby mode and send an error message with error code = REQUEST_CANCELED, when - The wake-up event register (wup_status) is not cleared - At least one EP is not idle - In at least one responder queue there is a message pending for transmission."

entries.title: Mode entry timing
entries.summary: The RC Server enters standby or sleep mode as soon as the go-to-sleep/standby response to the standby/sleep request has been sent.
entries.citation: p.56, "The RC Server enters standby or sleep mode, as soon as the go to sleep/standby response to the standby/sleep request has been sent."

entries.title: TC14/TC10 sleep request LPS confirmation gating
entries.summary: For a sleep request received via TC14/TC10 on the network, the same rejection conditions apply as for a normal sleep request; if the go-to-sleep conditions are not fulfilled, the network PHY shall not signal a TC14/TC10 LPS as confirmation.
entries.citation: p.56, "If the go to sleep conditions are not fulfilled the network PHY shall not signal a TC14/TC10 LPS as confirmation."

entries.title: RC Server discoverability
entries.summary: RC Servers shall be discoverable in the network via the defined "discovery request".
entries.citation: p.57, "RC Servers shall be discoverable in the network. Therefore a “discovery request” has been defined."

entries.title: Discovery response obligation
entries.summary: An RC Server may receive a discovery request in any lifecycle state and shall send a discovery response in return.
entries.citation: p.57, "An RC Server may receive a “discovery request” in any state of the life-cycle and shall send a “discovery response” in return."

entries.title: Discovery stream assignment and contention handling
entries.summary: The first discovery request received in HW_UNCONFIGURED or HW_CONFIGURED state sets the discovery stream for subsequent configuration requests; the stream is dropped after Discovery_TimeOut with no configuration activity; if multiple RC Clients send discovery requests, all receive the server_config map in response but only the first is allowed as the configuration stream, and configuration requests from others are rejected with an error response.
entries.citation: p.57, "only the first one will be allowed as configuration stream. If others send configuration requests they will be rejected and get an error response."

entries.title: Discovery request AVTPDU/ACF field values
entries.summary: Table 18 specifies the required field values for a discovery request: subtype=NTSCF, sv=1b, version=000b, stream_id = don't-care streamMAC + unique_id 0x0000, acf_msg_type=ACF_ABB, byte_bus_id=00000000000b, evt=0000b, op=1b (read), no byte_msg_payload.
entries.citation: p.57, Table caption: "Table 18: Discovery request"

entries.title: Discovery request header/format filtering
entries.summary: AVTPDUs having a TSCF header are dropped without further response, as well as discovery requests in ACF_GBB format.
entries.citation: p.57, "AVTPDUs having a TSCF header are dropped without further response, as well as requests in ACF_GBB format."

entries.title: Broadcast discovery request
entries.summary: A discovery request can be broadcast by an RC Client to detect all RC Servers on the network at once.
entries.citation: p.57, "A discovery request can be broadcasted by an RC Client to detect all RC Servers on the network at once."

entries.title: Discovery request frame addressing flexibility
entries.summary: A discovery request's Ethernet frame may have any DA, SA and VLAN tag, provided no MACsec is applied.
entries.citation: p.57, "A discovery request in an Ethernet frame may have any DA, SA and VLAN tag (if there is no MacSec applied)."

entries.title: Discovery response register-map content
entries.summary: The RC Server responds to a discovery request with the part of its register map starting from address 0x0000, with length determined by the read_size specified in the discovery request.
entries.citation: p.58, "The RC Server will respond with the part of the RC Server’s register map as starting from 0x0000 and its length being determined by the read_size in the discovery request."

entries.title: Client-side discovered-server cataloging
entries.summary: For each RC Server, the RC Client can read the register map fully or partially and maintain a table of relevant discovered RC Servers and their Endpoints, retrieving and configuring information from relevant Endpoints as needed by its application.
entries.citation: p.58, "the RC Client can read the register map full or partially and maintain a table of relevant discovered RC Servers and their endpoints"

entries.title: Persistent storage of discoverable information
entries.summary: Discoverable information (the RC Server's configuration) can be stored permanently in the RC Client for immediate availability at the next power-on, avoiding the need to re-run discovery when known a-priori.
entries.citation: p.58, "The discoverable information can be stored permanently in the RC Client for immediate availability at next power-on."

entries.title: Discovery response AVTPDU/ACF field values
entries.summary: Table 19 specifies the required field values for a discovery response: subtype=NTSCF, sv=1b, version=000b, stream_id = RC Server's localMAC + unique_id 0x0000, acf_msg_type=ACF_ABB, acf_msg_length ≤ read_size of the discovery request (capped at register-map size), byte_bus_id=00000000000b, evt=0000b, op=1b (read), byte_msg_payload = register-map content from address 0x00000.
entries.citation: p.58, Table caption: "Table 19: Discovery response"

entries.title: Discovery response Ethernet frame format
entries.summary: A discovery response is an Ethernet frame with DA set to the streamMAC from the discovery request's stream_id, SA set to the RC Server device MAC address, and no VLAN tag.
entries.citation: p.58, "A discovery response is an Ethernet frame that has DA = streamMAC from discovery request’s stream_id SA = RC Server device MAC address No VLAN tag."

entries.title: EP0-only access restriction pre-configuration
entries.summary: While the RC Server is in HW_UNCONFIGURED state, or before any valid stream_id/byte_bus_id combination has been defined, only access to EP0 is possible and only unconditional STANDARD requests are allowed; all other request types require a fully configured RC Server.
entries.citation: p.59, "only access to EP0 is possible and only unconditional STANDARD requests are allowed as all other request types need a full configured RC Server"

entries.title: REQUEST_REJECTED for disallowed EP0 requests
entries.summary: Any other valid request type sent to EP0 while EP0-only access restriction applies must be rejected with an error response carrying error code REQUEST_REJECTED.
entries.citation: p.59, "Other valid requests to EP0 will be rejected with an error response with error code REQUEST_REJECTED."

entries.title: Direct-to-EP configuration request preconditions
entries.summary: Configuration requests directly to EPs (not via EP0) are only allowed in RCP_CONFIGURED state, or in HW_CONFIGURED state with a valid stream_id/byte_bus_id configuration for that EP; if the condition is not fulfilled the request must be dropped.
entries.citation: p.59, "Configuration requests directly to EPs are only allowed. In RCP_CONFIGURED or in HW_CONFIGURED with valid stream_id/byte_bus_id configuration. If the condition is not fulfilled, the request is dropped."

entries.title: Register access-level enforcement (R/R-W*/R-W+/R-W)
entries.summary: Defines the four register access levels used throughout the register map and the write-enforcement each requires: R (read-only, no write), R/W* (write prohibited once lifecycle state is RCP_configured), R/W+ (write prohibited while svr_configuration_lock bit is set), and R/W (read/write at any time).
entries.citation: p.59, "R/W* :read access at any time, write access prohibited if in lifecycle state “RCP_configured”" / "R/W+ :read access at any time, write access prohibited if “svr_configuration_lock” bit is set"

entries.title: Direct EP_functional access via evt[2:0]=111b
entries.summary: An RC Client may access an endpoint's EP_functional configuration directly, without resolving the endpoint's base address in the RC Server's register map, by issuing a configuration request with evt[2:0] set to 111b.
entries.citation: p.59, "This can be done by setting evt[2:0] = 111b in request as described above."

entries.title: Configuration request message format
entries.summary: Figure 19 defines the Configuration request byte/message-info/payload layout: message-info byte holding acf_msg_type/acf_msg_length/pad/mtv/rsv/byte_bus_id; a byte with evt/rsv/hs/cs plus transaction_num, op/rsp/err/ms flags and read_size/segment_num; followed by a relative register start address within EP_func and the configuration data payload.
entries.citation: p.59, "Figure 19 – Configuration request"

entries.title: Configuration write payload truncation at EP_LEN
entries.summary: For a configuration write request, if the byte_msg_payload length plus the start_address would exceed the target endpoint's EP_LEN, the resulting out-of-range payload bytes must be ignored by the RC Server.
entries.citation: p.59-60, "Any byte_msg_payload for which the length plus the start_address results in a value larger than the EP_LEN, is to be ignored."

entries.title: HW_UNCONFIGURED configuration limited to discovery stream
entries.summary: While the RC Server is in HW_UNCONFIGURED lifecycle state, configuration is only possible via the discovery stream that was assigned in response to a discovery request; no other configuration access path is permitted.
entries.citation: p.59, "In HW_UNCONFIGURED state only configuration via the discovery stream assigned due to a discovery request is feasible."

entries.title: HW_CONFIGURED configuration access paths
entries.summary: In HW_CONFIGURED state, an RC Client may configure the device either through a discovery request and its discovery stream, or directly to endpoints via already-known stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations.
entries.citation: p.59, "In HW_CONFIGURED state configuration access can be either via a discovery request and the discovery stream or via know stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations directly to the EPs."

entries.title: Discovery-based reconfiguration disallowed once RCP_CONFIGURED
entries.summary: Once the RC Server reaches RCP_CONFIGURED state, configuration changes via a discovery request are no longer allowed.
entries.citation: p.59, "Changes in configuration via a discovery request are no longer allowed."

entries.title: Discovery requests still answered in RCP_CONFIGURED
entries.summary: Even though discovery-request configuration changes are disallowed in RCP_CONFIGURED state, the RC Server must nevertheless continue to answer discovery requests.
entries.citation: p.59, "Nevertheless, discovery requests are answered."

entries.title: RCP_CONFIGURED EP_functional config access restriction
entries.summary: In RCP_CONFIGURED state, EP_functional configuration access is only allowed via configured stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations addressed to the specific endpoint, or via the root client.
entries.citation: p.59, "Configuration to the EP functional config is only allowed via configured stream_id/byte_bus_id combinations to the EP or via the root client."

entries.title: RC Server register map, static/general part
entries.summary: Table 20 defines the RC Server register map's common read-only static part (addresses starting 0x0000): svr_oa_tc18_magic_nr, svr_version, svr_vendor_id, svr_device_id, svr_ep_count, svr_req_stream_max, svr_responder_streams_max, svr_responder_mem_size, svr_req_mem_size, svr_sequencers_max, svr_configuration_lock, svr_implemented_options (bit flags for compound&wait, trigger, chained, time-synch/timed, and enhanced-cancellation request support), svr_io_pin_count, and pointer/capacity pairs to the HW_config, request/response stream config, EP generic/functional config, EP-bytebus_id map, sequencer state, network interface, physical layer, time synch, security, and device-specific configuration register maps.
entries.citation: p.60-62, "Table 20: RC Server configuration static part"

entries.title: HW_config table writable only in HW_unconfigured
entries.summary: The HW_config (pin mapping) register map can only be changed while the RC Server is in the HW_unconfigured lifecycle state; in every other lifecycle state it is read-only.
entries.citation: p.63, "This configuration table can only be changed in the life-cycle state HW_unconfigured. In other states of the life cycle this is read-only."
