entries.title: Factory-default pin assignment and required configuration
entries.summary: By factory default, no endpoint signal is assigned to any physical IO-pin of the RCP PHY; the HW_config register map must be configured to establish pin-to-signal assignments and to define each IO-pin's electrical properties.
entries.citation: p.63, "As factory default there is no assignment of endpoint signals to physical IO-Pins of the RCP PHY. To make those assignments and also define the physical IO-Pin properties the HW_config register map needs to be configured."

entries.title: HW_config pin-mapping table layout
entries.summary: Table 21 defines the HW_config register map layout: a repeating 3-byte block per physical IO pin (hw_ep_nr, hw_ep_pin_nr, hw_pin_type), each field 8 bits wide with R/W* access, one block per IO pin up to the count given by svr_io_pin_count.
entries.citation: p.63, "Table 21: HW_config"

entries.title: Outputs are always also inputs
entries.summary: Any IO-pin configured as an output is always simultaneously usable/readable as an input as well.
entries.citation: p.64, "All outputs are always also an input."

entries.title: IO-pin properties (hw_pin_type) bitfield layout
entries.summary: Table 22 defines the hw_pin_type byte bitfield: bits[1:0] Pull-Up (00 float, 01 pull-down, 10 pull-up), bits[3:2] Output stage (00 input, 01 open-drain, 10 open-source, 11 push-pull), bits[5:4] Drive strength (00 input, 01 low, 10 medium, 11 high), bit 6 reserved (reads 0), bit 7 Schmitt-Trigger enable (0=no hysteresis, 1=hysteresis applied).
entries.citation: p.64, "Table 22: IO-pin properties"

entries.title: Enumeration of EP_Pin_Nr signals per endpoint type
entries.summary: Table 23 enumerates the per-endpoint-type EP_Signal_Nr assignments referenced by hw_ep_pin_nr: GPIO (pins 0-31), SPI (SPI_CLK, SPI_PICO, SPI_POCI, SPI_CS n for 0<=n<16), I2C (I2C_SCL, I2C_SDA), UART (UART_TX, UART_RX, UART_RTS, UART_CTS), LIN (LIN_TXD, LIN_RXD, LIN_NSLP), PWM_OUT (positive/inverted phase), PWM_IN, ADC, DAC, CAN (RXD, TXD), ISELED (ISP_P, ISP_N), and MDIO (MDC clock, MDIO data).
entries.citation: p.65, "Table 23: Enumeration of signals at endpoints"

entries.title: Request stream configuration register map
entries.summary: Defines the RC Server's request-stream register layout (offsets 0x0000 onward) including rx_stream_id, rx_stream_max_request_size, rx_wd_timeout_intervall, rx_secure_channel_index, the rx_enforce_crc/sequence/watchdog/request_filing control bits, rx_stream_status, rx_safestate_seqencer, rx_safe_sequencer_state, rx_ack_stream_index and rx_resp_stream_index, repeated per additional request stream (Request stream 2 begins at 0x0018).
entries.citation: p.66-67, Table 24: Request stream configuration

entries.title: Request stream config table writable only outside RCP_CONFIGURED
entries.summary: Table 24 (Request stream configuration) can only be changed in life-cycle states HW_UNCONFIGURED and HW_CONFIGURED; once in RCP_CONFIGURED it is read-only, matching its W* R/W marking.
entries.citation: p.67, 'This configuration table can only be changed in the life-cycle states HW_UNCONFIGURED and HW_CONFIGURED. In RCP_CONFIGURED of the life cycle this is read-only. (As indicated by W*)'

entries.title: EP_ID_config register map
entries.summary: Defines the stream-endpoint-byte_bus_id mapping structure: repeated Request_Stream_IndexN (8bit), EP_NrN (8bit), BBIDN (11bit) and CtrlN (5bit) entries that map a request stream to specific endpoints via byte_bus_id.
entries.citation: p.68, Table 25: EP_ID_config (Request_stream & byte_bus_id mapping to Endpoints and their channels)

entries.title: BBID control bits (x_Ctrl) layout
entries.summary: Defines the 5-bit x_Ctrl field: bit 4 CRC_required (0b=without CRC, 1b=with CRC) and bits 3:0 Channel_selection selecting the EP channel to handle the request (applicable to SPI EP when multiple CS lines are supported).
entries.citation: p.68, Table 26: BBID control bits

entries.title: EP0 access always CRC protected
entries.summary: When EP_Nr=0 is configured, the CRC_required bit is don't-care because access to EP0 must be CRC protected in all cases regardless of the configured bit value.
entries.citation: p.68, '** in case EP_Nr = 0 (access to EP0 is configured), then CRC_required is “don’t care” since access to EP0 needs to be CRC protected in any case'

entries.title: Request_Stream_Index=0 marks EP_ID_config table end
entries.summary: A Request_Stream_Index value of 0 in the EP_ID_config table denotes the end of the table (list terminator); default values otherwise allow access to EP0.
entries.citation: p.68, 'The default values allow to access EP0. A Request_Stream_Index = 0 denotes the end of the table.'

entries.title: EP_ID_config table lockable against modification
entries.summary: The EP_ID_config configuration table can be locked to protect against unwanted modification, as indicated by its W+ R/W marking.
entries.citation: p.68, 'This configuration table can be locked by to protect against unwanted modification, as indicated by W+.'

entries.title: Ascending order of Request_Stream_Index/BBID entries
entries.summary: The Request_Stream_Index and BBID parameters shall occur in ascending order in the EP_ID_config table; the sender of the configuration must ensure this ordering, since incorrect ordering can cause requests to be dropped (no EP found).
entries.citation: p.68, 'The parameters Request_Stream_Index and BBID shall occur in ascending order. This has to be ensured by the instance that is sending the configuration to this table.'

entries.title: RC Client may use multiple streams for one endpoint
entries.summary: One RC Client may use multiple streams to address the same endpoint, resulting in multiple entries in its client_config.
entries.citation: p.68, 'One RC Client may use multiple streams to address the same endpoint, so will have multiple entries in the client_config.'

entries.title: Endpoint should be used by only one RC Client at a time
entries.summary: For safety reasons it is recommended that one endpoint is only used by one RC Client at a time.
entries.citation: p.68, 'For safety reasons it is recommended that one endpoint is only used by one RC Client at a time.'

entries.title: Stream may address multiple EPs sharing a BBID
entries.summary: A stream may address multiple endpoints on different RC Servers, or on the same RC Server, that share the same byte_bus_id.
entries.citation: p.68, 'A stream may address multiple EPs on different RC Servers or on the same RC Server having the same byte_bus_id.'

entries.title: RC Client must configure at least one stream-BBID entry per endpoint
entries.summary: The RC Client is responsible for configuring at least one stream-byte_bus_id combination for each endpoint it uses.
entries.citation: p.69, 'The RC Client is responsible for configuring at least one stream-byte_bus_id combination for each endpoint.'

entries.title: Endpoints sharing a BBID in one stream should be same type
entries.summary: If multiple endpoints are configured to use the same byte_bus_id inside one stream, they should be of the same type.
entries.citation: p.69, 'If multiple endpoints are using the same byte_bus_id inside one stream they should be of the same type.'

entries.title: Duplicate EP/BBID/stream entries cause N-fold request filing
entries.summary: If N entries assign the same EP to the same BBID within the same stream, an incoming request may be filed N times into that endpoint's request storage.
entries.citation: p.69, 'If there are N entries assigning the same EP to the same BBID in the same stream, then requests may be filed N-times to the addressed Eps request storage.'

entries.title: Max_AVTPDUsize must be configurable and discoverable
entries.summary: The maximum length of an AVTPDU sent by the RC Server shall be configurable, to avoid sending very long frames, and this maximum must be discoverable in the RC Server Info/Config register map.
entries.citation: p.70, 'The maximum length of an AVTPDU sent by the RC Server shall be configurable to be able to avoid sending very long frames and is discoverable in the RC Server Info/Config register map.'

entries.title: Max_AVTPDUsize must not exceed network MTU
entries.summary: Max_AVTPDUsize shall always be configured such that the resulting network frame does not exceed the network's maximum transmit unit size.
entries.citation: p.70, 'The Max_AVTPDUsize shall always be configured such that the final network frame does not exceed the maximum transmit unit size of the network.'

entries.title: Fragmentation via ACF_ABB/ACF_GBB ms-bit when exceeding Max_AVTPDUsize
entries.summary: When an AVTPDU containing a single ACF_type would exceed Max_AVTPDUsize, fragmentation as supported in ACF_ABB and ACF_GBB via the ms-bit shall be performed.
entries.citation: p.70, 'In case an AVTPDU containing a single ACF_type would exceed the \"Max_AVTPDUsize\" fragmentation as supported in ACF_ABB and ACF_GBB by the ms-bit will be performed.'

entries.title: flush_on_count triggers queue transmission with size-fitted packing
entries.summary: Once a response/ack queue holds a quadlet count equal to or greater than flush_on_count, transmission of one or more AVTPDUs shall be initiated; each generated AVTPDU includes only as many ACF_types as fit Max_AVTPDUsize, and all pending ACF_types (including the one that exceeded the threshold) are transmitted across a fitting number of AVTPDUs.
entries.citation: p.70, 'Once a queue is filled with an amount of quadlets that is equal or larger than given by \"flush_on_count\", the transmission of one or multiple AVTPDUs shall be initiated.'

entries.title: Flush_time triggers queue transmission
entries.summary: Transmission of an AVTPDU from a queue shall also be initiated when the time elapsed since the last transmission from that queue is equal to or greater than Flush_time.
entries.citation: p.70, 'The transmission of an AVTPDU shall be initiated also in case the time since the last transmission from this queue is equal or greater than the Flush_time.'

entries.title: Heartbeat AVTPDU generated on empty-queue Flush_time timeout
entries.summary: Even when the response/ack queue is empty, an AVTPDU shall be generated on Flush_time expiry to act as a heartbeat so the RC Client can detect the RC Server is alive.
entries.citation: p.70, 'An AVTPDU shall be generated in this case even when the queue is empty to generate a heartbeat, so that the RC Client sees that the RC Server is alive.'

entries.title: Responder QUEUE_config register map
entries.summary: Defines the per-responder-queue register layout: STREAM_UID (16bit, upper stream-id bits), Max_AVTPDUsize (16bit), queue_size (16bit, in 32bit words), flush_on_count (16bit, count threshold or immediate), and Flush_time (16bit, microseconds or count-only), repeated per Responder Queue (Queue 1 at 0x0000, Queue 2 at 0x000A, etc.).
entries.citation: p.70, Table 27: Responder QUEUE_config

entries.title: Sequencer dedicated to a single RC Client
entries.summary: Each sequencer is dedicated to a specific RC Client and its bound endpoints, i.e. sequencer state/access is scoped to one client rather than shared across clients.
entries.citation: p.71, 'Each sequencer is dedicated to a specific RC Client and its bound endpoints.'

entries.title: Sequencer state power-on reset value
entries.summary: Upon power-on reset, all sequencer state values shall be set to \"1\".
entries.citation: p.71, 'Upon power-on reset all sequencer state values are set to “1”.'

entries.title: Sequencer implementation is optional
entries.summary: Implementation of one or more sequencers into an RC Server is optional; whether the feature is available, and how many sequencers exist, is discoverable in the RC Server's register map.
entries.citation: p.71, 'The implementation of one or more sequencers into an RC Server is optional.'

entries.title: SEQUENCER_config register map
entries.summary: Defines the per-sequencer register layout: Seq_state (8bit, current state, default 1, manually setting 0 disables the sequencer) and Request_stream_index (8bit R/W*, refers to the Client Nr allowed to access this sequencer), repeated per sequencer instance (Seq_1, Seq_2, Seq_3, ...).
entries.citation: p.71, Table 28: SEQUENCER_config

entries.title: Network interface config section address range
entries.summary: The network interface configuration section is defined to start at register address svr_network_interface_cfg_ptr and span to svr_network_interface_cfg_ptr + svr_network_interface_cfg_capacity.
entries.citation: p.72, 'This configuration section starts at register address svr_network_interface_cfg_ptr and spans to svr_network_interface_cfg_ptr + svr_network_interface_cfg_capacity.'

entries.title: Ethernet interface section comprises entire MAC configuration
entries.summary: In case of an Ethernet interface, the network interface configuration section shall comprise the entire MAC configuration.
entries.citation: p.72, 'In case of an Ethernet interface this section comprised the entire MAC configuration.'

entries.title: Physical layer config section address range
entries.summary: The physical layer configuration section is defined to start at register address svr_physical_layer_cfg_ptr and span to svr_physical_layer_cfg_ptr + svr_physical_layer_cfg_capacity.
entries.citation: p.72, 'This configuration section starts at register address svr_physical_layer_cfg_ptr and spans to svr_physical_layer_cfg_ptr + svr_physical_layer_cfg_capacity.'

entries.title: MDIO Manageable Devices may leave physical layer section empty
entries.summary: In case of \"MDIO Manageable Devices\" the physical layer configuration section might be empty, with physical layer access instead possible via an MDIO endpoint.
entries.citation: p.72, 'In case of “MDIO Manageable Devices” this section might be empty and the access to the physical layer might be possible via an MDIO endpoint.'

entries.title: Time synch config section address range
entries.summary: The time synchronization configuration section is defined to start at register address svr_time_synch_cfg_ptr and span to svr_time_synch_cfg_ptr + svr_timesynch_cfg_capacity.
entries.citation: p.72, 'This configuration section starts at register address svr_time_synch_cfg_ptr and spans to svr_time_synch_cfg_ptr + svr_timesynch_cfg_capacity.'

entries.title: Security config section address range
entries.summary: The security configuration section is defined to start at register address svr_security_cfg_ptr and span to svr_security_cfg_ptr + svr_security_cfg_capacity.
entries.citation: p.72, 'This configuration section starts at register address svr_security_cfg_ptr and spans to svr_security_cfg_ptr + svr_security_cfg_capacity.'

entries.title: PLCA slot configuration for 10BASE-T1S
entries.summary: When the RC Server's network interface is 10BASE-T1S, one or more PLCA slots in which the RC Server is allowed to send must be configured.
entries.citation: p.73, §12.8.1: 'In case the network interface is 10BASE-T1S one or more PLCA slots have to be configured in that the RC Server is allowed to send.'

entries.title: Discard non-gPTP/non-IEEE1722 frames
entries.summary: A received frame that is found to be neither a gPTP frame nor an IEEE1722 frame shall be discarded by the RC Server.
entries.citation: p.73, §12.8.2: 'If neither a gPTP nor an IEEE1722 frame is found the received frame shall be discarded.'

entries.title: Stream_id lookup and request filing
entries.summary: Once an IEEE1722 AVTPDU is handed to the RC Server, it checks the stream_id and, if known, extracts the contained requests and files them into the addressed Endpoints' request storages.
entries.citation: p.73, §12.8.2: 'The RC Server checks the stream_id and if known to the RC Server extracts the contained requests and files them in the addressed Endpoints request storages.'

entries.title: Fragmentation reassembly via ACF_GBB/ACF_ABB
entries.summary: Fragmentation as supported by ACF_GBB/ACF_ABB must be accounted for by the RC Server on reception in order to reconstruct complete requests.
entries.citation: p.73, §12.8.2: 'Fragmentation as supported by ACF_GBB/ACF_ABB needs to be considered to get complete requests.'

entries.title: Minimum inter-frame reception timing
entries.summary: The RC Server shall be able to receive and handle frames with a minimum time between frames/packets (e.g. the Ethernet minimum interpacket gap).
entries.citation: p.73, §12.8.2: 'The RC Server shall be able to receive and handle frames with a minimum time between the frames/packets. E.g. for ethernet the minimum interpacket gap.'

entries.title: Drop request on unmatched byte_bus_id/stream_id
entries.summary: If the lookup of the byte_bus_id in the context of the stream_id does not resolve to a known Endpoint, the request must be dropped without further notification.
entries.citation: p.74, §12.9.1: 'If the lookup of the byte_bus_id in the context of the stream_id does not point to an Endpoint, the request is dropped without further notification.'

entries.title: RC Server as configurable endpoint
entries.summary: For configuration purposes the RC Server itself is treated as an endpoint and may have, within each configured stream_id, its own byte_bus_id, defaulting to zero.
entries.citation: p.74, §12.9.1: 'For configuration purposes the RC Server itself is also treated as an endpoint. It may have within each configured stream_id an own byte_bus_id, which is zero as a default.'

entries.title: Requests delivered to addressed endpoint request storage
entries.summary: Requests are delivered by the RC Server to the request storage of the addressed Endpoint(s), per the execution priority rules of §12.9.2.
entries.citation: p.74, §12.9.1: 'Requests are delivered by the RC Server to the request storage of the addressed Endpoint(s) (see section \"Priorities in execution\").'

entries.title: Responder/acknowledge queues 1:1 to stream_id
entries.summary: The RC Responder must provide several responder and acknowledge queues, each assigned 1:1 to a stream_id (and thus to a destination, which can be a multicast destination).
entries.citation: p.74, §12.9.1: 'The RC Responder will provide several responder- and acknowledge queues that are assigned 1:1 to a stream_id (and with that to a destination which can also be a multi-cast destination).'

entries.title: Per-endpoint responder/ack queue configuration
entries.summary: Each Endpoint can be configured as to which responder and acknowledge queue its responses and acknowledges shall be routed to, depending on the stream from which the request was received.
entries.citation: p.74, §12.9.1: 'Each Endpoint can be configured to which responder and acknowledge queue its responses and acknowledge shall go in dependence of the stream from which the request was received.'

entries.title: EP may send acknowledge on queuing
entries.summary: As soon as a request has been filed into an addressed endpoint's request storage and is scheduled for execution, the EP may send an acknowledge, subject to configuration.
entries.citation: p.74, §12.9.1: 'As soon as the request has been filed in one of the addressed endpoint request storages and therefore is scheduled for execution, the EP may send an acknowledge (which depends on configuration)'

entries.title: Read response payload on op=0
entries.summary: A response with payload data read from the EP is given after execution of a request when requested via op=0 (read request).
entries.citation: p.74, §12.9.1: 'A response with pay load data read from the EP is given, if requested by op=0 (read request) after the request has been executed.'

entries.title: Write response err=0 on success unless suppressed
entries.summary: After successful execution of a write request (op=1), a response with err=0 and no payload is given unless suppressed via EP_GENERIC_config.
entries.citation: p.74, §12.9.1: 'A response with err=0 and no payload is given after successful execution of a request with op=1 (write request) as long as not configured to be suppressed within the EP_GENERIC_config.'

entries.title: Error response err=1 with error_code unless suppressed
entries.summary: If a request could not be executed for any reason, a response with err=1 and an error_code in byte_msg_payload is sent, unless suppressed via EP_GENERIC_config.
entries.citation: p.74, §12.9.1: 'If a request could not be executed for any reason, a response with err=1 is sent and an error_code in the byte_msg_payload is given as long as not configured to be suppressed within the EP_GENERIC_config'

entries.title: Response/ack association via byte_bus_id and transaction number
entries.summary: Responses and acknowledges are associated to their originating requests by the byte_bus_id and transaction number.
entries.citation: p.74, §12.9.1: 'Response(s) and acknowledge(s) are associated to the requests by the byte_bus_id and transaction number.'

entries.title: UNSUPPORTED_CMD error when evt[2:0]!=0 with no payload
entries.summary: If evt[2:0] is nonzero and no byte_msg_payload is present, an error response shall be sent with error_code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD.
entries.citation: p.74, §12.9.1: 'If evt[2:0] ≠ 0 and no byte_msg_payload is present, then an error response shall be sent with the error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD'

entries.title: Frame may include multiple ACF-types
entries.summary: An RCP frame may include multiple ACF-types (requests) within a single AVTPDU.
entries.citation: p.74, §12.9.1.1: 'An RCP frame may include multiple ACF-types (requests).'

entries.title: Support multiple requests per frame
entries.summary: An RC Server shall support handling multiple requests within one frame, checking each individually for byte_bus_id/stream_id match and filing matched requests into the corresponding endpoint request storages.
entries.citation: p.74, §12.9.1.1: 'An RC Server shall support handling multiple requests in one frame and check each of them individually if to be processed or not (byte_bus_id/stream_id match) and files the requests into the corresponding request storage of the endpoints.'

entries.title: Single presentation-time regime per frame
entries.summary: Because an AVTPDU carries either a TSCF or NTSCF header, a mixture of requests with and without presentation time cannot occur in one frame; a TSCF header's presentation time is applied to all ACF-types within that frame.
entries.citation: p.74, §12.9.1.1: 'a mixture of requests with and without presentation time in a single frame is not possible. A presentation time from a TSCF header will be applied to all ACFtypes within the frame.'

entries.title: Support multiple request types in one frame
entries.summary: The RC Server shall support handling of multiple different request types (e.g. Standard, Trigger, Compound with/without WAIT) within a single frame.
entries.citation: p.74, §12.9.1.1: 'The RC Server shall support the handling of multiple request types in one frame.'

entries.title: Endpoint checks EP request storage for due requests
entries.summary: Whenever an Endpoint is able to start a new request, it shall check all requests in the EP request storage for whether they are due for execution.
entries.citation: p.75, §12.9.2: 'Whenever an Endpoint is able to start a new request, it shall check for all requests in the EP request storage whether they are due for execution.'

entries.title: TSCF request due earliest at presentation time
entries.summary: A request received under a TSCF header is due for execution earliest at its presentation time.
entries.citation: p.75, §12.9.2: 'A request received under TSCF header is due earliest at the presentation time.'

entries.title: Execution priority order across request types
entries.summary: When two or more requests are simultaneously due for execution, priority is resolved in the fixed order: cancellation, triggered, timed, compound, compound wait, chained, standard.
entries.citation: p.75, §12.9.2: 'In case two or more requests are due for execution then the priorities are as follows: 1. cancellation 2. triggered 3. timed 4. compound 5. compound wait 6. chained 7. standard'

entries.title: Same-priority requests execute in arrival order
entries.summary: When two or more due requests share the same priority level, execution shall start in the order in which the requests arrived in the EP request storage.
entries.citation: p.75, §12.9.2: 'When two or more requests with the same priority are due then starting the execution shall happen in the order with which the requests arrived in the EP request storage.'

entries.title: Request lifecycle states (pending/RS/RE/RF)
entries.summary: A filed request moves through the states "request pending" → "request started" (RS, pending any execution delay) → "request under execution" (RE) → "request finalized" (RF); in RF the request is deleted if remaining repetitions is zero, else the repetition count is decremented unless configured for unlimited repetitions.
entries.citation: p.76, §12.9.3: 'Once a request has been filed into an EP request storage, it is in the state "request pending"... The lifecycle advances to "request under execution" (RE)... and then to "request finalized" (RF)...'

entries.title: Table 29: Execution procedure
entries.summary: Defines the start-and-execution procedure at RS/RE/RF for each request type (Cancellation, Triggered, Timed request, Compound request, Compound wait request, Chained request, Standard request), including exec-delay timers, sequencer state transitions (cmp_sequencer/cmp_next_state/cmp_start_state), and repetition/removal rules.
entries.citation: p.76-77, Table 29: 'Execution procedure'

entries.title: Trigger condition/delay independent of EP idle state
entries.summary: For trigger requests specifically, the fulfillment of the trigger condition and the start of the trigger delay time shall be independent of whether the endpoint is idle.
entries.citation: p.77, §12.9.3: 'Especially for trigger requests the fulfillment of the trigger condition and start of the trigger delay time shall be independent of the idle state of the endpoint.'

entries.title: EP request storage overflow handling
entries.summary: When an EP request storage is full, newly arriving requests are dropped and responses with the corresponding error code are generated; avoiding such overflow is the responsibility of the RC Client.
entries.citation: p.77, §12.9.3: 'When an EP request storage is full, newly arriving requests are dropped and responses with the corresponding error code generated. It is the duty of the RC Client to avoid such overflow.'

entries.title: Responder queues 1:1 to stream_id
entries.summary: The RC Responder must provide several responder queues, each assigned 1:1 to a stream_id (RC Server's MAC address + 16-bit unique stream_id) and a destination address, which may be multicast.
entries.citation: p.78, §12.9.4: 'The RC Responder will provide several responder queues that are assigned 1:1 to a stream_id (RC Servers's MAC address + 16bit unique stream_id) and a destination address which can also be a multicast destination.'

entries.title: RC Client responder-queue configuration per endpoint
entries.summary: Each RC Client has a configuration determining via which responder queue requests to an Endpoint shall generate responses.
entries.citation: p.78, §12.9.4: 'Each RC Client has a configuration via which responder queue requests to Endpoint shall generate responses.'

entries.title: Response format ACF_GBB vs ACF_ABB by timestamp config
entries.summary: When an Endpoint is configured to timestamp responses, the response is sent in ACF_GBB format; otherwise it is sent in ACF_ABB format.
entries.citation: p.78, §12.9.4: 'When the Endpoint is configured to timestamp responses, then the response will be in ACF_GBB, otherwise in ACF_ABB format.'

entries.title: Responses associated by transaction number
entries.summary: The Endpoint provides responses to the RC Responder associated with their requests via the request's transaction number.
entries.citation: p.78, §12.9.4: 'The Endpoint provides responses associated with the requests identified by the transaction number of the request to the RC Responder.'

entries.title: Single response evt[3:0]=0x0
entries.summary: When a request generates exactly one response, that response's evt[3:0] field equals 0x0.
entries.citation: p.78, §12.9.4: 'In case a request generates exactly one response, then this response has evt[3:0] = 0x0.'

entries.title: Multi-response evt[3:0] counter
entries.summary: When more than one response is generated (e.g. repetitive trigger or compound operation), evt[3:0] carries a counter incremented per response so the RC Client can detect loss of responses; the RC Client is responsible for counting responses to determine when the transaction_num can be released.
entries.citation: p.78, §12.9.4: 'the evt[3:0] includes a counter (see section 11.3 Responses) that is incremented for each response, so that the RC Client is able to detect loss of responses. The RC Client is responsible for counting the responses to determine when the transaction_num can be released.'

entries.title: Response queue overflow handling
entries.summary: If a response queue is completely full when a new response is delivered, the AVTPDU with the lowest sequence_num must be evicted to make room, and the overflow bit shall be set so the RC Client can detect the missing sequence_num.
entries.citation: p.78, §12.9.4: 'the AVTPDU with the lowest sequence_num has to be removed from the queue to make space for the new response. The overflow bit in the respective shall be set. The RC Client will detect a missing sequence_num.'

entries.title: Acknowledge sent on successful queuing
entries.summary: An acknowledge, if requested, is given as soon as a new request has been successfully queued for execution in the addressed endpoint's request storage.
entries.citation: p.78, §12.9.5: 'An acknowledge is given if requested as soon as the new request has been successfully queued for execution in the addressed endpoints request storage.'

entries.title: Acknowledge association and stream routing
entries.summary: The acknowledge is associated to its request by the request's transaction number and is sent via the stream associated to the request stream for acknowledges.
entries.citation: p.78, §12.9.5: 'The acknowledge is associated to the request by the transaction number of the request and is sent via the stream that has been associated to the request stream for acknowledges.'

entries.title: Acknowledge queue overflow handling
entries.summary: If an acknowledge queue is completely full when a new acknowledge is delivered, the AVTPDU with the lowest sequence_num must be evicted to make room, and the overflow bit shall be set so the RC Client can detect the missing sequence_num.
entries.citation: p.78, §12.9.5: 'the AVTPDU with the lowest sequence_num has to be removed from the queue to make space for the new acknowledge. The overflow bit in the respective shall be set. The RC Client will detect a missing sequence_num.'

entries.title: Endpoints generate error responses
entries.summary: Endpoints generate error responses depending on execution errors or HW failures (e.g. an output pin could not be driven to the desired state), as governed by the RC Server's capabilities.
entries.citation: p.79, §12.9.6: 'Endpoints will generate error responses depending on execution errors or HW failures (e.g. an output pin could not be driven to the desired state) depending on the RC Servers' capabilities.'

entries.title: Error responses configurable timestamping
entries.summary: Endpoints shall be configurable to timestamp error responses.
entries.citation: p.79, §12.9.6: 'Endpoints shall be configurable to timestamp error responses.'

entries.title: Error response content requirements
entries.summary: The error response shall contain the byte_bus_id and transaction number of the originating request, and shall contain a byte_msg_payload carrying an error code.
entries.citation: p.79, §12.9.6: 'The error response shall contain the byte_bus_id and transaction number of the request. The error response shall contain a byte_msg_payload with an error code.'

entries.title: Table 30: Error codes in responses
entries.summary: Defines the 17 error codes and values used in byte_msg_payload of error responses: UNSUPPORTED_CMD(1), SEQUENCER_NOT_KNOWN(2), UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS(3), LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS(4), REQUEST_CANCELED(5), REQUEST_NOT_FOUND(6), EP_ERROR(7), EP_NOT_FOUND(8), PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL(9), REQ_storage_OVFL(10), REQUEST_REJECTED(11), POCI_FAILURE(12), PRESENTATION_TIME_TOO_FAR(13), GPTP_FAIL(14), INVALID_PARAMETER(15), CHAIN_ABORTED(16), CHAIN_ERROR(17), each with a description.
entries.citation: p.79, Table 30: 'Error codes in responses'

entries.title: Sequencers reset to state 1 on power-on
entries.summary: After power-on/reset, all sequencers are in state 1.
entries.citation: p.80, §12.10: 'After power-on/reset all sequencers are in state 1.'

entries.title: Sequencer state read/control via RC Server
entries.summary: The state of the sequencers can be read out via the RC Server, and enabling, disabling, and setting the sequencer state are likewise controlled via the RC Server (see §12.7.10 Sequencer state registers).
entries.citation: p.80, §12.10: 'The state of the sequencers can be read out via the RC Server. Also enabling, disabling, as well as setting the sequencer state is controlled via the RC Server.'

entries.title: Sequencer/state count limited to 256
entries.summary: The number of sequencers and the number of states per sequencer are limited to 256 by this specification.
entries.citation: p.80, §12.10: 'The number of sequencers and states per sequencer are limited to 256 by this definition.'

entries.title: Implementation may support fewer sequencers
entries.summary: An RC Server implementation may support only a lower number of sequencers than the 256 maximum permitted by the specification.
entries.citation: p.80, §12.10: 'An RC Server implementation may support only a lower number of sequencers.'

entries.title: Request routing by STREAM_ID and byte_bus_id
entries.summary: Requests without a known STREAM_ID are discarded by the RC Server. byte_bus_id is only unique within the context of a STREAM_ID, and a request is only passed to an endpoint if both the STREAM_ID and byte_bus_id match.
entries.citation: p.81, "Requests not having a known STREAM_ID are discarded by the RC Server. The byte_bus_id is only unique in the context of a STREAM_ID and requests are only passed to the endpoint if both match."

entries.title: Unused endpoint has no pin mapping or validation role
entries.summary: When EP_USED in EP_config is 0, the endpoint has no mapping to HW pins and is not used to validate any requests.
entries.citation: p.81, "If it is not used (EP_USED bit in EP_config set to 0) then there is no mapping to HW pins, and the endpoint is not used to validate any requests."

entries.title: Endpoint enable/disable request-storage processing
entries.summary: A used endpoint may be enabled or disabled: when enabled it processes requests from its request storage; when disabled, processing stops and the RC Client may preload the storage for execution once the endpoint is re-enabled.
entries.citation: p.81, "If enabled, it starts processing requests from its request storage. If disabled, the processing is stopped, and the RC Client can e.g. preload the storage with a sequence of requests to executed as soon as the endpoint gets enabled."

entries.title: ROOT_CLIENT-exclusive write access to server config
entries.summary: When a ROOT_CLIENT is configured in SERVER_config, only the ROOT_CLIENT has write access to all RC Server configuration register maps; other RC Clients get write access only to EP_functional configuration of endpoints allocated to them in EP_ID_config.
entries.citation: p.81, "If within the RC Server's SERVER_config the ROOT_CLIENT is configured only the ROOT_CLIENT has write access to all RC Server configuration register maps. For other RC Clients than the ROOT_CLIENT write access is only given to EP_functional configuration of endpoints which are allocated to the RC Client within the EP_ID_config register map."

entries.title: ep_generic_config register map
entries.summary: Defines the fixed generic (common) register block replicated per endpoint instance (EP0, EP1, ...): ep_type (8-bit R, index into TYPE matrix), ep_used (1-bit R/W*, fixed to 1 for EP0), ep_delay_time (2-bit R/W*: 00b=1us,01b=10us,10b=20us,11b=50us), ep_req_storage_size (16-bit R/W*, storage size in 32-bit words), ep_description (32-bit R/W*, user-defined text), ep_tx_buffer_size and ep_rx_buffer_size (16-bit R/W* each, buffer size in 32-bit words; reads 0x0000 if the endpoint has no such buffer).
entries.citation: p.82, Table 31 caption: "Table 31: ep_generic_config register map"

entries.title: ep_type enumerated values
entries.summary: Enumerates the 8-bit ep_type values identifying endpoint kind: 0x00 Server(EP0), 0x01 WakeUp, 0x02 GPIO, 0x03 SPI, 0x04 I2C, 0x05 UART, 0x06 LIN, 0x07 PWM_OUT, 0x08 PWM_IN, 0x09 ADC, 0x0A DAC, 0x0B CAN, 0x0C ISELED, 0x0D MDIO.
entries.citation: p.83, Table 32 caption: "Table 32: ep_type values"

entries.title: Error response must reference error-causing pin
entries.summary: When EP_RESP_ON_ERROR-enabled IO-pin gauging detects that a set IO pin's state does not follow, an error is flagged and the response shall include the reference to the error-causing pin; for other error sources (e.g. wrong sequencer addressed) an error response with the corresponding error code is generated instead.
entries.citation: p.82, "The response shall include the reference to the error causing pin. If the source of an error is a different type (e.g. wrong sequencer addressed) an error response with a corresponding error code is generated."

entries.title: Presentation time ignored when time sync unsupported
entries.summary: If the RC Server does not support time synchronization, a presentation time carried in a TSCF-headed AVTPDU shall be ignored, and the request(s) executed as if no presentation time were included, or dropped, depending on RC Server configuration.
entries.citation: p.84, "In case the RC Server does not support time synchronization, the presentation time shall be ignored, and the request(s) executed as if no presentation time were included or dropped depending on the configuration of the RC Server."

entries.title: Invalid timestamp (tv=0) ignored
entries.summary: For requests in a TSCF-headed AVTPDU whose timestamp is marked invalid (tv=0), the timestamp is ignored.
entries.citation: p.84, "For requests sent in an AVTPDU having a TSCF header with the time stamp marked as invalid (i.e. tv = 0), the timestamp is ignored."

entries.title: All-zero reserved header bytes queued as NTSCF or dropped
entries.summary: If the reserved bytes in the TSCF header are all zero, the request shall be queued as if the header were in NTSCF format, or dropped, depending on RC Server configuration.
entries.citation: p.84, "If the reserved bytes in the header are all zero, then the request shall be queued as if the header was in NTSCF format or dropped, depending on configuration."

entries.title: Uncertain timestamp (tu=1) treated as tu=0
entries.summary: When the timestamp is marked uncertain (tu=1), the request shall be executed as if tu=0.
entries.citation: p.84, "In case the time stamp is uncertain (i.e. tu = 1), then this shall be executed as if tu = 0."

entries.title: EP-specific usage of evt-field
entries.summary: Defines per-endpoint-type semantics of evt[2:0] in requests: for SPI, 000b-101b select interface channel 0-5 and assert the associated CSN pin, 110b is reserved (reject UNSUPPORTED_CMD), 111b reconfigures the endpoint instead of presenting the payload; for ADC/PWM_IN/I2C/LIN/CAN/UART/ISELED/MDIO, 000b-110b are reserved (reject UNSUPPORTED_CMD) and 111b reconfigures the endpoint; for GPIO/PWM_OUT, 000b writes payload directly, 001b/010b/011b perform bitwise OR/AND/XOR with current interface status, 100b is reserved (ignored, error response UNSUPPORTED_CMD), 101b/110b add/subtract payload to/from current status, and 111b reconfigures the endpoint.
entries.citation: p.86, Table 33 caption: "Table 33: EP specific usage of evt-field"

entries.title: evt[3] acknowledge-request bit semantics
entries.summary: evt[3] is used to request an acknowledge: evt[3]=1 requests an acknowledge for the request, independent of the endpoint-type-specific meaning of evt[2:0].
entries.citation: p.86, "evt[3] is used to request an acknowledge. I.e. evt[3] = 1 requests acknowledge."

entries.title: Saturation arithmetic for GPIO/PWM_OUT add/subtract
entries.summary: For the GPIO/PWM_OUT evt=101b (add) and evt=110b (subtract) operations, neither overflow nor wrap-around shall occur; results are saturated at 0x0000 on the low side and 0xFFFF on the high side.
entries.citation: p.86, "While doing additions and subtractions neither overflows nor wrap-arounds shall occur. The values are saturated at 0x0000 on the low side and 0xFFFF at the high side."

entries.title: Compound-wait byte-length mismatch handling
entries.summary: In compound-wait requests, if the interface status has fewer bytes than byte_msg_payload the wait condition never becomes true; if the interface status has more bytes than byte_msg_payload, the interface status shall be capped to the length of byte_msg_payload before comparison (e.g. for SPI only the first 4 of 20 received bytes are checked against a 4-byte payload).
entries.citation: p.87, "In case the interface status has less bytes than the byte_msg_load, the wait condition never comes true. If the interface status has more bytes than the byte_msg_payload, then the interface status shall be capped to the length of the byte message payload."

entries.title: Compound-wait evt-field comparison semantics
entries.summary: Defines the compound-wait evt[2:0] comparison modes: 000b exact match; 001b all '1' bits in payload must be '1' in status (bit-set test); 010b all '1' bits in payload must be '0' in status (bit-clear test); 011b reserved, request shall be ignored and an UNSUPPORTED_CMD error response shall be sent; 100b/101b greater-or-equal / less-or-equal compare of the first two bytes of the first quadlet (e.g. PWM_in period); 110b/111b greater-or-equal / less-or-equal compare of the last two bytes of the first quadlet (e.g. PWM_in duty cycle).
entries.citation: p.87, "evt[2:0] = 000b – wait condition is met when byte_msg_payload matches exactly as is to interface status" ... "evt[2:0] = 011b - reserved - request shall be ignored and an err-response with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD shall be sent"

entries.title: Safe command mode CRC mismatch handling
entries.summary: If a request is received by an endpoint in Safe command mode and its CRC does not match, the request is not executed and an error response with error code CRC_ERROR is generated; depending on configuration (rx_enforce_crc, §12.7.7) additional safety measures might be taken.
entries.citation: p.88, "If a request is received by an endpoint that is in “Safe command mode” and the CRC does not match, the request is not executed, and an error response is generated with error code: CRC_ERROR. Depending on configuration safety measures might be taken (see parameter rx_enforce_crc in 12.7.7 Request stream configuration)."

entries.title: CRC32 calculation scope in Safe command mode
entries.summary: In Safe command mode a CRC32 is calculated per ACF type across specific fields of the AVTPDU header, the ACF header, and the entire payload (excluding padding).
entries.citation: p.88, "In Safe command mode a CRC32 is calculated per ACF type across specific fields of an AVTPDU header, ACF header, and the entire payload (except padding)."

entries.title: CRC32P4 polynomial parameters
entries.summary: Defines the CRC32P4 used for end-to-end protection: polynomial 0xF4ACFB13, width 32 bit, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF (for header CRC calculation), final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF (applied to ACF CRC result), input reflection TRUE, output reflection TRUE.
entries.citation: p.88, Table 34 caption: "Table 34: CRC32 Polynomial"

entries.title: ACF_ABB under TSCF header CRC field layout
entries.summary: Depicts the AVTPDU/ACF_ABB field layout for CRC calculation under a TSCF header: fields marked orange in the TSCF header shall be used to calculate a header CRC, which seeds the per-ACF-type CRC calculation; the ACF_ABB CRC (blue) covers the fields marked green, and the resulting CRC32 is appended into the byte_msg_payload (with stack-added padding).
entries.citation: p.88, Figure 20 caption: "Figure 20: ACF_ABB under TSCF header (example)"; "The fields marked in orange in the TSCF header shall be used to calculate a header CRC, which is then used are seed value for the calculation of the individual CRCs of each ACF type under this header."

entries.title: ACF_GBB under NTSCF header CRC field layout
entries.summary: Depicts the AVTPDU/ACF_GBB field layout for CRC calculation under an NTSCF header: fields marked orange in the NTSCF header shall be used to calculate a header CRC used as seed value for the per-ACF-type CRC; the ACF_GBB CRC (blue) covers the fields marked green, appended into byte_msg_payload with stack-added padding.
entries.citation: p.89, Figure 21 caption: "Figure 21: ACF_GBB under NTSCF header (example)"; "The fields marked in orange in the NSCF header shall be used to calculate a header CRC, which is then used are seed value for the calculation of the individual CRCs of each ACF type under this header."

entries.title: acf_msg_length accounting for appended CRC
entries.summary: When calculating the CRC, it must be considered that appending the CRC to byte_msg_payload increases acf_msg_length by 1.
entries.citation: p.89, "When calculating the CRC, it needs to be considered that adding the CRC to the byte_msg_payload increases the acf_msg_length by 1."

entries.title: CRC computed once, before fragmentation
entries.summary: Fragmentation, if applied to a message, happens after CRC calculation, so the CRC is calculated only once and is transmitted in the last segment.
entries.citation: p.89, "Fragmentation, if applied to a message, happens after CRC calculation. So, the CRC is only calculated once and will be transmitted in the last segment."

entries.title: Identical CRC scheme for requests and responses
entries.summary: The CRC calculation for requests and for responses follows the identical scheme.
entries.citation: p.89, "The CRC calculation for requests and responses follows the identical scheme."

entries.title: EP functional config common entries (ep_enable&clr, ep_options)
entries.summary: Defines the common functional-configuration register block shared by all endpoint types, spanning two bytes referred to as ep_enable&clr and ep_options: ep_enable (1-bit R/W, default 1 enabled except EP0 always enabled), ep_clear_req_storage (1-bit R/W, write-1 clears the endpoint's request storage, reads 0), ep_req_crc_enable (1-bit R/W*, CRC required on incoming frames / safe mode), ep_ack_crc_enable (1-bit R/W*, CRC generated for acknowledges), ep_response_crc_enable (1-bit R/W*, CRC generated for responses), ep_response_ts_enable (1-bit R/W*, insert timestamp in response), ep_error_stream (1-bit R/W*, selects response vs. acknowledge stream for error responses), ep_ack_ts_enable (1-bit R/W*, insert timestamp in acknowledge), ep_supress_error_msgs (1-bit R/W*, suppress response on error), ep_supress_response (1-bit R/W*, suppress response on successful write). Margin comments on ep_req_crc_enable and ep_response_crc_enable flag them (051RC5, TI_066) as leftover fields to be removed since CRC use is now configured per-stream rather than per-endpoint.
entries.citation: p.90, Table 35 caption: "Table 35: EP functional config common entries"

entries.title: RC Server config storage and access path
entries.summary: The RC Server's configuration is stored in the SERVER_config register map (not the EP_functional configuration, since the RC Server itself is excluded from it); the register map is accessed for read/write by the RC Client via ACF_ABB using the server's configured byte_bus_id, which defaults to zero.
entries.citation: p.91, "Therefore, the RC Server as endpoint is not included in the EP_functional configuration." / "...via ACF_ABB with the servers configured byte_bus_id (which is by default zero)."

entries.title: RC Server cyclic heartbeat
entries.summary: The RC Server shall support sending a cyclic heartbeat, achieved by configuring a response queue with fixed periodicity; if that queue is empty, an empty PDU (NTSF header only, no acf_types) is sent instead.
entries.citation: p.91, "The server shall support sending a cyclic heartbeat."

entries.title: Trigger request as heartbeat alternative
entries.summary: As an alternative to a periodic response queue, a trigger request may be queued (if supported) to cyclically generate responses carrying the read result from a status or diagnostic register.
entries.citation: p.91, "Alternatively, a trigger request - if supported- can be queued that cyclically generates responses with the read result from a status or diagnostic register."

entries.title: RC Server functional configuration register map
entries.summary: Defines the RC Server EP0 functional-configuration register fields: svr_ep_len, reserved, svr_ep_enable&clr, svr_ep_options, svr_root_client_index, svr_lifecycle_state (0x00 HW_UNCONFIGURED / 0x55 HW_CONFIGURED / 0xAA RCP_CONFIGURED), svr_discovery_timeout (16-bit, µs, default 20000), and svr_ep_status, each with relative address, bit width and R/W access.
entries.citation: p.91, Table 36: "RC Server functional configuration"

entries.title: svr_root_client_index write-access scope
entries.summary: svr_root_client_index selects the request stream that, while the server is in HW_CONFIGURED, retains write access to all registers of the register map (0 = no stream has root access); write requests to EP0 arriving via any other stream are limited to EP0 and must not affect other endpoints.
entries.citation: p.91, "Write requests to EP0 via all other streams are limited to EP0 and not beyond (i.e. other EPs)."

entries.title: ACF_ABB RC Server register write (safe mode)
entries.summary: Depicts the ACF_ABB byte-message layout used to write the RC Server's register map in safe command mode: header fields (acf_msg_type/length/pad/mtv/ACK/CFG/byte_bus_id, evt/rsv/hs/cs, transaction_num/op/rsp/err/ms, read_size/segment_num) followed by register start address, write data, and a 32-bit CRC with padding.
entries.citation: p.91, Figure 22 - "ACF_ABB for RC Server register write access in safe mode" (annotated 051RC5: figure updated to 32bit CRC)

entries.title: EP0 register-write payload format
entries.summary: The write-access payload to EP0 consists of a 16-bit register start address, the data to be written, and a CRC; EP0 is always accessed in safe command mode so the CRC is mandatory on every such request.
entries.citation: p.92, "The payload consists of a 16-bit address, the data to be written to the address and a CRC, since EP0 is always accessed in safe command mode."

entries.title: Effective register-write byte-count formula
entries.summary: The number of payload bytes actually written to the register map is computed as (acf_msg_length - 3) x 4 - pad - 2, accounting for header, pad and CRC overhead.
entries.citation: p.92, "Effective number of bytes to be written to register map = (acf_msg_length - 3) x 4 – pad -2." (051RC5: Formular corrected)

entries.title: evt[2:0] register-write bit operation
entries.summary: Handling of write data for an EP0 register access depends on evt[2:0]: the payload bits are either SET, OR'ed, AND'ed or XOR'ed into the target register's content.
entries.citation: p.92, "The handling of the data depends on evt[2:0] so that the bits are either SET, OR'ed, AND'ed or XOR'ed to the target registers content."

entries.title: Register-write edge-case and error behavior
entries.summary: A write with payload 0x00000000 and evt=0x001 (OR) results in no effect; writes to read-only registers are accepted with no effect and confirmed normally; writes to a write-prohibited register (e.g. a map-set lock bit) are rejected with err=1 and error code UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS.
entries.citation: p.92, "Writing to a write prohibited register (e.g. lock bit for map set) creates a response with err = 1 and an error code UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS."

entries.title: Config register-map addressing and EP sequence
entries.summary: Each _config register map is addressed via its base address plus the relative address given in its own _config map description; for EP_functional configuration, the ordering of per-endpoint functional descriptions is determined by the endpoints' sequence in EP_GENERIC_config.
entries.citation: p.92, "For the EP_functional configuration the sequence of the functional descriptions of the endpoints is determined by their sequence in the EP_GENERIC_config."

entries.title: RC Server trigger signals
entries.summary: Lists trigger signals an RC Server may optionally generate: 0 = PTP time-sync established (if PTP supported), 1 = PTP time-sync lost (if PTP supported), 2 = t.b.d.
entries.citation: p.92, Table 37: "Trigger signals issued by an RC Server"

entries.title: Example RC Server configuration (placeholder)
entries.summary: Intended to show a worked-example EP_functional configuration for a 3-endpoint system (GPIO, PWM_OUT, ADC) plus wake-up/sleep endpoint; in this revision the table body is unpopulated, marked "TABLE TO BE UPDATED" — implementers cannot cite concrete values from it yet.
entries.citation: p.92, Table 38: "Example of an RC Server configuration" (body: "TABLE TO BE UPDATED")

entries.title: WakeUp endpoint fixed at EP nr 1
entries.summary: The WakeUp endpoint is a special endpoint fixed to endpoint number 1, being the only endpoint that stays active while the RC Server implementation is in sleep mode.
entries.citation: p.93, "The WakeUp endpoint is a special endpoint and as this fixed to the endpoint nr 1, as it is the only endpoint which stays active in Sleep mode of the RC Server implementation."

entries.title: Repetitive wake-up messages after reconnection
entries.summary: After the WakeUp endpoint wakes the RC Server and a network connection is re-established, the WakeUp endpoint sends repetitive messages at a configurable interval (flush_time).
entries.citation: p.93, "After establishing a network connection, the WakeUp endpoint sends repetitive messages. The timing interval is configurable (flush_time)."

entries.title: WakeUp IO-pin mapping and debounce
entries.summary: The WakeUp endpoint requires a configured mapping of the IO pins it listens to for wake-up, and a debounce time is specified for the signals to suppress spurious wake-up on noise.
entries.citation: p.93, "The WakeUp EP needs a mapping of the IO-Pins it listens to wake up. A debounce time for the signals is specified to suppress wake-up on noise."

entries.title: WakeUp functional configuration register map
entries.summary: Defines the WakeUp EP1 functional-configuration registers: wup_ep_len, wup_nr_io_pins_max (max gaugeable IO pins), wup_ep_status (16-bit), wup_status (16-bit, one bit per wake-up source, write-1-to-clear), and a repeating wup_io_scrN entry (16-bit: [10:0] IO pin number, [15:11] IO behavior) list terminated by a pin number of 0.
entries.citation: p.93, Table 39: "wake-up control - functional configuration"

entries.title: WakeUp source pin IO_SRC encoding
entries.summary: Defines the IO_SRC[15:11] pin-behavior encoding used in wup_io_scrN: 00000 pin inactive, 00001 rising edge, 00010 falling edge, 00011 both edges, 00100 high level, 00101 low level, all other combinations reserved.
entries.citation: p.94, Table 40: "wake-up source pin configuration"

entries.title: Client-initiated sleep request
entries.summary: To bring the RC Server implementation into sleep mode, the RC Client has to send a specific request to the WakeUp endpoint.
entries.citation: p.94, "To bring the RC Server implementation into sleep mode the RC Client has to send a specific request to the WakeUp endpoint."

entries.title: RC Server sleep-entry sequence
entries.summary: On receiving the sleep request the RC Server must: (1) stop entering incoming requests into endpoint queues; (2) have EPs signal that no pending execution-time-base or standard requests remain queued; (3) once all EPs are idle and all responder queues are empty (all responses sent), send a sleep-request acknowledge and then transition the RC Server implementation to sleep mode.
entries.citation: p.94, "Based on the sleep request the RC Server will: 1. stop entering incoming requests into endpoint queues. ... send an acknowledge to sleep request; bring the RC Server implementation to sleep mode."

entries.title: WakeUp endpoint sleep request format
entries.summary: Depicts the byte-level message structure of the WakeUp endpoint sleep request sent by the RC Client to initiate server sleep mode.
entries.citation: p.94, Figure 23 - "Endpoint sleep request"

entries.title: SleepCMD fixed code value
entries.summary: The SleepCMD field used in the WakeUp endpoint sleep request message is coded as the fixed value 0xA5.
entries.citation: p.94, "SleepCMD is coded as 0xA5."

entries.title: SPI channel selection via byte_bus_id mapping
entries.summary: For each byte_bus_id, the Request_stream & byte_bus_id-to-endpoint mapping (defined in Table 25, EP_ID_config, outside this page range) shall determine which channel of the SPI EP handles the request. Multiple byte_bus_ids from one or multiple streams can address the same SPI endpoint.
entries.citation: p.95, "...Table 25: EP_ID_config...includes configuration which channel of the EP shall handle the request. Mind that multiple byte_bus_ids from one or multiple streams can address the same endpoint."

entries.title: Up to 16 pre-configurable SPI configuration sets
entries.summary: An SPI endpoint may support up to 16 pre-configurable sets of SPI configurations (for parallel-SPI bus devices with differing communication settings), selected in an SPI request via the evt-field / byte_bus_id.
entries.citation: p.95, "the SPI endpoint may support up to 16 pre-configurable sets of SPI configurations, which are selected in a SPI request via the evt-field. byte_bus_id."

entries.title: Client byte-send request to SPI endpoint
entries.summary: The RC Client can request the SPI endpoint to send one or more bytes, delivered as byte_msg_payload of an ACF_ABB/GBB, with execution being immediate (asap), timed, or conditional.
entries.citation: p.95, "The RC Client can request the SPI endpoint to send one or more bytes...The execution of this request might be \"immediate\"(asap), \"timed\" or \"conditional\"."

entries.title: SPI requests accepted in ACF_ABB/ACF_GBB
entries.summary: SPI endpoint requests are accepted in the ACF_ABB and ACF_GBB message formats.
entries.citation: p.95, "Requests are accepted in ACF_ABB and ACF_GBB."

entries.title: Optional SPI wait-for-bit-sequence request
entries.summary: The Client can optionally request the SPI endpoint to wait until a pre-defined bit sequence has been received from the connected device; the byte_msg_payload of the wait-request is compared against the last data received, irrespective of which CS channel was used.
entries.citation: p.95, "Optionally the Client can request the SPI endpoint to wait until a pre-defined bit sequence has been received...compared against the last data received (irrespective of which CS channel was used)."

entries.title: Optional SPI HW trigger event generation
entries.summary: An SPI endpoint optionally creates HW trigger events, depending on the physical interface implementation.
entries.citation: p.95, "An SPI endpoint optionally creates the following HW trigger events depending on physical interfaces implementation:"

entries.title: SPI trigger outputs mapping
entries.summary: Table 41 defines the SPI endpoint's HW trigger-signal-to-event mapping: signal 0 = SPI execution done, 1 = reserved, (2+2n) = CSn asserted, (3+2n) = CSn de-asserted, for 0<=n<16.
entries.citation: p.95, Table 41 caption: "spi trigger outputs"

entries.title: SPI functional register access can be locked
entries.summary: Access to the SPI EP functional configuration registers, reached via RC Server EP_functional configuration, can be locked in the generic endpoint configuration.
entries.citation: p.96, "The access to the functional parameters can be locked in the generic endpoint configuration."

entries.title: SPI functional configuration register map
entries.summary: Table 42 defines the SPI EP functional-configuration register map: spi_ep_len, spi_nr_cs (4-bit, supported CS count-1, max 16 CS), spi_ep_enable&clr, spi_ep_options, spi_ep_status, and per-channel SPI_CFGn blocks (spi_baud_rate0 in kbit/s, spi_clk_polarity0, spi_clk_phase0, spi_cs_polarity0, spi_use_cs0, spi_deassert_cs_pause, spi_cs_clk_leadtime0, spi_clk_cs_trailtime0, spi_bits_max0, spi_pause_min0), repeated as SPI_CFG1 etc. for additional channels.
entries.citation: p.96-97, Table 42 caption: "spi functional configuration" (rows incl. "spi_nr_cs...Number of supported CS / configurations -1 (max 16 CS)")

entries.title: SPI R/W register parameters runtime-changeable
entries.summary: All SPI functional-configuration parameters marked R/W-type can be changed at runtime.
entries.citation: p.97, "All parameters marked of R/W-type can be changed at runtime."

entries.title: SPI pause is an optional feature
entries.summary: Support of SPI pause is optional; if not supported, spi_bits_max0 and spi_deassert_cs_pause are fixed to 0.
entries.citation: p.97, "Support of SPI pause is an optional feature. If not supported, then spi_bits_max0 and spi_deassert_cs_pause are fixed to 0."

entries.title: SPI pause timing behavior when supported
entries.summary: When SPI pause is supported and spi_bits_max0 > 0, the clock signal pauses after every spi_bits_max0 bits for a duration of spi_cs_clk_leadtime0 + spi_pause_min0 + spi_clk_cs_trailtime0 clock cycles; if spi_deassert_cs_pause = 1, CS is de-asserted during the pause window from spi_cs_clk_leadtime0 until spi_cs_clk_leadtime0 + spi_pause_min0.
entries.citation: p.97, "In case of spi_bits_max0 >0, then clock signal pauses after every spi_bits_max0 for a number of clock cycles that equals spi_cs_clk_leadtime0 + spi_pause_min0 + spi_clk_cs_trailtime0."

entries.title: Parallel SPI: up to 6 CS configurations, selected via evt[2:0]
entries.summary: For a parallel SPI structure, up to 6 CS signals may be handled by the SPI endpoint via its configurations; the SPI bus functional configuration supports up to 6 different configurations in parallel, with the configuration used per request determined by evt[2:0]. Note: this "up to 6" figure appears inconsistent with the "up to 16" configuration-set / CS count stated elsewhere in this section (§13.7.3.1, and spi_nr_cs field description in Table 42, "max 16 CS"); an editorial marker on this text notes it is "to be updated if new concept is accepted," suggesting a stale/unreconciled value.
entries.citation: p.98, "up to 6 CS signals may be handled by the SPI endpoint via its configurations...the SPI bus functional configuration supports up to 6 different configurations in parallel. Which configuration is used within an SPI request is determined by evt[2:0]."

entries.title: Single-CS interface requires external de-multiplexing
entries.summary: If the physical interface implementation supports only one CS signal, de-multiplexing to individual SPI devices needs to be done outside the SPI EP, either via an external GPIO-controlled demux or by using GPIOs directly as CS pins asserted/de-asserted by (e.g.) trigger requests from the single SPI CS.
entries.citation: p.98, "If the interface implementation just supports one CS the de-muxing to the individual SPI devices needs to be done outside the SPI EP."

entries.title: SPI EP retains last received data for wait-operation
entries.summary: Because the SPI endpoint can wait for configurable input data to trigger a compound operation, it needs to keep the last received data internally available for the wait-operation comparison, up to the length of read_size defined in the acf-type.
entries.citation: p.98, "it needs to keep the last received data internally available for checking (wait-operation) up to the length of the read_size defined with the acf-type."

entries.title: SPI error state on execution stop
entries.summary: If the SPI EP stops execution (per cs/hs bits), the endpoint enters error state (reflected in spi_ep_status) and its enable bit in EP_config is reset; the RC Client must clear the error status and re-enable the endpoint to resume operation.
entries.citation: p.98, "then SPI endpoint is in error state...The error status needs to be cleared (by the RC Client) and the endpoint needs to be enabled again to continue operation."

entries.title: Client can clear SPI EP queues before continuing
entries.summary: The Client can decide to clear one or more queues of the SPI endpoint before continuing operation, e.g. after an error.
entries.citation: p.98, "The Client can also decide to clear one or more queues of this endpoint before continuing operation."

entries.title: Clamped SPI pin diagnostic flag
entries.summary: A clamped SPI pin (stuck at VDD/GND, latching, etc.) shall raise a flag in the server's diagnostic registers and set the \"error\" flag in all responses of that endpoint.
entries.citation: p.98, "A clamped pin shall raise a flag in the server's diagnostic registers and set the \"error\" flag in all responses of this endpoint."

entries.title: SPI request message layout example
entries.summary: Figure 24 shows an example SPI request byte layout (evt=0101b, transaction_num, op/rsp/err/ms, byte_bus_id, read_size=0x0A, byte_msg_payload) illustrating a write of 20 bytes with a 10-byte response on SPI channel 3.
entries.citation: p.98, Figure 24 caption: "SPI request (example to write 20 bytes and get a response with 10 on SPI channel 3)"

entries.title: SPI EP zero-pads short payload for read_size
entries.summary: The SPI EP shall append zeros when read_size is larger than the number of bytes present in the byte_msg_payload.
entries.citation: p.98, "The SPI EP shall append zeros in case the read_size is larger than the number of bytes in the byte_msg_payload."

entries.title: Full byte_msg_payload presented on PICO regardless of read_size
entries.summary: The full byte_msg_payload is presented on PICO even when read_size is less than the number of bytes contained in the byte_msg_payload.
entries.citation: p.98, "The byte_msg_payload will be presented on PICO in full, even if the read_size is less than the number of bytes in the byte_msg_payload."

entries.title: GPIO EP supports up to 32 IOs
entries.summary: Each GPIO endpoint can handle up to 32 IOs, providing access to digital input and output pins.
entries.citation: p.99, "Each GPIO endpoint can handle up to 32 IOs."

entries.title: Per-pin direction and drive strength configurable
entries.summary: For each GPIO pin the direction (input/output) can be configured; for each pin configured as output, the drive strength can also be configured.
entries.citation: p.99, "For each pin the direction (input/output) can be configured. For each pin configured as output the drive strength can be configured."

entries.title: Per-pin output drive mode configurable
entries.summary: For each pin configured as output, it can be configured whether the drive mode is push-pull, open-drain, or open source.
entries.citation: p.99, "For each pin configured as output it can be configured, if this is push-pull, open-drain or open source."

entries.title: GPIO bit-mapping rule for EPs with fewer than 32 pins
entries.summary: Each GPIO pin is assigned to a bit position of the byte_msg_payload; when the EP supports fewer than 32 pins, the least-significant bits of the payload are used for the mapping.
entries.citation: p.99, "In case the EP supports less than 32 pins, the least-significant bits are used."

entries.title: GPIO request length validation
entries.summary: A GPIO request not having exactly four bytes is rejected, and an error response with error code = INVALID_PARAMETER is sent.
entries.citation: p.99, "A request not having exactly four bytes is rejected and an error response with error code = INVALID_PARAMETER will be sent."

entries.title: GPIO request message layout example
entries.summary: Figure 25 shows an example GPIO request byte layout for a 24-pin EP, mapping IO0-IO23 bit positions within the byte_msg_payload (remaining upper bits don't-care).
entries.citation: p.99, Figure 25 caption: "GPIO request (example for EP with 24 pins)"

entries.title: GPIO output set / logical-operation change
entries.summary: Output pins can be set to a defined state, and the current state can be changed via a logical operation (NAND, OR, XOR).
entries.citation: p.99, "Output pins can be set to a defined state and the current state can be changed by a logical operation (NAND, OR, XOR)."

entries.title: Pulse generation is not a GPIO EP function
entries.summary: Generating a pulse for a defined time is NOT a function of the GPIO endpoint; this must instead be managed by the Client (e.g. sending two commands, optionally with presentation times) via a compound or trigger operation.
entries.citation: p.99, "Generating a pulse for a defined time is NOT a function of the GPIO endpoint. This either needs to be managed by the Client...by a compound or a trigger operation."

entries.title: GPIO EP can be triggered by another endpoint
entries.summary: The GPIO Endpoint can also be triggered by another endpoint to generate a response.
entries.citation: p.99, "The GPIO Endpoint can also be triggered by another endpoint to generate a response."

entries.title: GPIO requests accepted in ACF_ABB/ACF_GBB
entries.summary: GPIO endpoint requests are accepted in the ACF_ABB and ACF_GBB message formats.
entries.citation: p.99, "Requests are accepted in ACF_ABB and ACF_GBB."

entries.title: Optional GPIO edge/change trigger generation
entries.summary: The GPIO endpoint optionally generates triggers for all its mapped IO pins on change, falling, and rising edge; the trigger reference numbers are built so that change/rising/falling events for a given GPIO are always sequential.
entries.citation: p.99, "The GPIO endpoint optionally generates triggers for all its mapped IO-pins on the change, falling and rising edge."

entries.title: GPIO trigger outputs mapping
entries.summary: Table 43 defines the GPIO endpoint's HW trigger-signal-to-event mapping: signal 0 = GPIO EP request execution done, then sequential triples per IOn (signal change, rising edge, falling edge) from IO0 up to IO31 falling edge at signal 96.
entries.citation: p.99, Table 43 caption: "gpio trigger outputs" (rows incl. "0 GPIO EP request execution done".."96 IO31 falling edge")

entries.title: GPIO functional configuration register map
entries.summary: Table 44 defines the GPIO EP functional-configuration register map: gpio_ep_len, gpio_io_max (max supported IO pin number), gpio_ep_enable&clr, gpio_ep_options, gpio_base_clk (16-bit, kHz), gpio_ep_status, gpio_clk_divider, and per-pin gpio_debounce_IO0...gpio_debounce_IO31 (8-bit each; 0 = no debounce, n>0 = n consecutive same-value samples required before output changes, sampled per gpio_base_clk/gpio_clk_divider independent of requests).
entries.citation: p.100, Table 44 caption: "gpio functional configuration" (row: "gpio_debounce_IO0...n>0 : n consecutive samples of the same value need to be sampled, before the output value is changed")

entries.title: GPIO R/W register parameters runtime-changeable
entries.summary: All GPIO functional-configuration parameters of R/W-type can be changed at runtime.
entries.citation: p.100, "All parameters of R/W-type can be changed at runtime."

entries.title: All request formats valid for GPIO EPs
entries.summary: All defined request formats are valid for GPIO EPs.
entries.citation: p.100, "All defined request formats are valid for GPIO EPs."

entries.title: GPIO WAIT request semantics and trigger basis
entries.summary: A WAIT request assesses the internal GPIO read register against the WAIT condition carried in the byte_msg_payload of the request; the GPIO endpoint generates its trigger events based on the physical state of the IO pins.
entries.citation: p.100, "A WAIT request assesses the internal GPIO read register versus the WAIT condition in the byte_msg_payload of the request. a GPIO endpoint generates the trigger events based on the physical state of the IO Pins"

entries.title: Zero-data OR request results in no change
entries.summary: A GPIO request with data 0x00000000 and evt[2:0] = 0x001 (OR logical operation) results in \"no change\" to the outputs.
entries.citation: p.100, "A request with data \"0x0000 0000\" and evt[2:0] = 0x001 (OR) results in \"no change\"."

entries.title: Write to input pin is ignored
entries.summary: A write request targeting a pin configured as an input is ignored for that pin.
entries.citation: p.100, "A write request to an input pin is ignored for this input pin."

entries.title: GPIO response delivery via responder queues
entries.summary: The server collects delivered GPIO responses and acknowledges them in the configured responder queues, sending them according to the responder queue configuration.
entries.citation: p.100, "The server collects the delivered responses and acknowledges in the configured responder queues and sends them according to the configuration of the responder queues."

entries.title: Pure GPIO read generates immediate response
entries.summary: A read request without a byte_msg_payload (pure read) generates a response immediately upon execution.
entries.citation: p.100, "A read request without a byte_msg_payload (pure read) generates a response immediately upon execution."

entries.title: GPIO read-with-payload/write waits for debounce before response
entries.summary: A read request that includes a byte_msg_payload, as well as a write request, first changes the drive of the pins, then waits for the debounce time before creating a response.
entries.citation: p.100, "A read request with a byte_msg_payload as well as a write request first change the drive of the pins, then wait for the debounce time before creating a response."

entries.title: PWM_OUT primary output pin required
entries.summary: For each PWM_OUT endpoint, at least a first (primary) output pin must be configured in the HW_config; this is the only mandatory pin for the endpoint.
entries.citation: p.102, "For each PWM_OUT endpoint at least a first output pin needs to be configured in the HW_config."

entries.title: PWM_OUT inverted output pin optional
entries.summary: Use of an inverted PWM signal is optional; a second output pin with opposite phase to the first output pin may optionally be configured for a PWM_OUT endpoint.
entries.citation: p.102, "The use of the inverted PWM signal is optional... a second output pin can be configured which has the opposite phase of the first output pin."

entries.title: PWM_OUT inverted-edge delay for break-before-make
entries.summary: When an inverted output pin is configured, the delay between the rising edges of the primary and inverted outputs may be defined in clock cycles of the PWM source clock, supporting 'break before make' behavior in half-/full-bridge drivers; the delayed signal is used for trigger signal generation.
entries.citation: p.102, "the delay of the rising edges of the primary and inverted output can be defined in clock cycles of the PWM source clock. This is to support 'break before make' behavior in half- and full bridge drivers."

entries.title: pwmo signals timing diagram
entries.summary: Figure 26 illustrates the PWM_OUT primary and inverted output signal relationship, including phase and the configurable rising-edge (skew) delay.
entries.citation: p.102, "Figure 26 – pwmo signals"

entries.title: PWM_OUT request payload length validation
entries.summary: A PWM_OUT request whose payload is not exactly four bytes must be rejected, and an error response with error code = INVALID_PARAMETER shall be sent.
entries.citation: p.104, "A request not having exactly four bytes is rejected and an error response with error code = INVALID_PARAMETER will be sent."

entries.title: PWM_OUT start/stop semantics
entries.summary: A PWM_OUT request starts continuous PWM signal generation on the assigned output pin(s) until stopped; to stop PWM signal generation a request with PWM_Period of '0' shall be issued.
entries.citation: p.104, "To stop PWM signal generation a request with PWM_Period of '0' shall be issued."

entries.title: PWM_OUT active=0, period>0 behavior
entries.summary: A request with PWM_active = 0 and PWM_Period > 0 keeps the PWM endpoint active with the output disabled, while trigger signals are still generated.
entries.citation: p.104, "With a request with PWM_active = 0 and PWM_Period > 0 the PWM remains active, however, the output is disabled, but trigger signals are still generated."

entries.title: PWM_OUT trigger-configuration request field semantics
entries.summary: When the request is a trigger configuration, the first two bytes of byte_msg_payload state the phase shift (not the period), enabling the PWM output to be synchronized with a fixed phase relation to another PWM_OUT endpoint.
entries.citation: p.104, "In case the request is a trigger configuration, the first two bytes of the byte_msg_payload state the phase shift (and not the period)."

entries.title: PWM_OUT output toggle self-check
entries.summary: During PWM generation the output pin is also used as an input and checked that it actually toggles; if it does not toggle, an error shall be signaled.
entries.citation: p.104, "During PWM generation the output pin will also be used as input and checked that they really toggle. If not, an error shall be signaled."

entries.title: PWM_IN max-period exceeded / source-loss error notification
entries.summary: If the incoming signal's period exceeds the configured maximum allowed period, or the external PWM source stops, the PWM_IN endpoint detects this and, when enabled via EP_config (EP_RESP_ON_ERR), notifies the RC Client with an error response message.
entries.citation: p.105, "If the period of the incoming signal exceeds the configured maximum allowed period or if the external PWM source stops, the PWM_IN endpoint will detect this and if enabled within the EP_config (EP_RESP_ON_ERR) notify the RC Client with an error response message."
