entries.title: I2C EP drives a single bus
entries.summary: The I2C endpoint is defined as an I2C controller that drives exactly one I2C bus; the spec does not provide for multi-bus operation from a single I2C EP instance.
entries.citation: p.108, §13.7.7.1: 'The I2C endpoint is an I²C controller. It drives a single I²C bus.'

entries.title: Client-initiated I2C byte send via ACF_ABB/ACF_GBB
entries.summary: The Client may request the I2C endpoint to send one or more bytes, delivered as byte_msg_payload of an ACF_ABB to the endpoint (detailed in Annex M of IEEE1722b); such requests are accepted in both ACF_ABB and ACF_GBB message types.
entries.citation: p.108, §13.7.7.1: 'The Client can request the I²C endpoint to send one or more bytes that are delivered as byte_msg_payload of an ACF_ABB... Requests are accepted in ACF_ABB and ACF_GBB.'

entries.title: Optional I2C wait-for-bit-sequence request
entries.summary: The Client may optionally request the I2C endpoint to wait until a pre-defined bit sequence has been received from a connected I2C device, i.e. a compound-wait style request is optional functionality for this EP type.
entries.citation: p.108, §13.7.7.1: 'Optionally the Client can request the I²C endpoint to wait for a pre-defined bit sequence has been received from a connected device.'

entries.title: I2C functional configuration register map
entries.summary: Table 49 defines the I2C EP's functional configuration register layout: i2c_ep_len(0x0000,8b,R), Reserved(0x0001,8b), i2c_ep_enable&clr(0x0002,8b,R/W), i2c_ep_options(0x0003,8b,R/W*), i2c_base_clk(16b,R) also shown at address 0x0002, i2c_ep_status(0x0004,16b,R/W), i2c_clock_divider(0x0006,8b,R/W), i2c_mode(0x0007,8b,R/W, encoding 0=Standard 100kbit/s,1=Fast 400kbit/s,2=Fast+ 1Mbit/s,3=High-speed listed twice as both 1.7Mbit/s and 3.4Mbit/s,4=Ultra-fast 5Mbit/s), and i2c_trail(0x0008,8b,R/W, minimum trail time between transactions). NOTE: as extracted, i2c_base_clk and i2c_ep_enable&clr both show relative address 0x0002, and the i2c_mode value 3 is documented twice with two different data rates (1.7Mbit/s and 3.4Mbit/s) — a likely table/address inconsistency worth flagging against any implementation's register map citation.
entries.citation: p.108-109, Table 49: 'i2c functional configuration' (address column shows i2c_ep_enable&clr and i2c_base_clk both at 0x0002; i2c_mode value '3' listed twice as 'High-speed mode 1.7Mbit/s' and 'High-speed mode 3.4Mbit/s')

entries.title: I2C R/W parameters runtime-changeable
entries.summary: All parameters of R/W type in the I2C functional configuration (Table 49) may be changed at runtime, i.e. runtime reconfiguration of I2C EP parameters is permitted without requiring an EP disable/re-init cycle.
entries.citation: p.109, §13.7.7.2: 'All parameters of R/W-type can be changed at runtime.'

entries.title: I2C request format diagram
entries.summary: Figure 30 illustrates the I2C request byte_msg_payload format via a worked example of an I2C transfer using a 10-bit address with 5 bytes of data, showing how the address (of unspecified 7- or 10-bit width, since the EP is transparent to address width) is embedded transparently in the payload.
entries.citation: p.108-109, Figure 30 – 'i2c request format'

entries.title: Optional I2C HW trigger event generation
entries.summary: An I2C endpoint may optionally generate hardware trigger events, as enumerated in Table 50, rather than being required to support triggers.
entries.citation: p.109, §13.7.7.4: 'An I²C endpoint optionally generates HW trigger events'

entries.title: UART EP dual independent TX/RX request storages
entries.summary: Because UART transmission and reception are independent processes, the UART EP must implement two separate EP request storages: one dedicated to transmitting data and one dedicated to receiving data.
entries.citation: p.110, §13.7.8.1: 'these two processes are independent from each other, thus the UART EP has two EP request storages, one for transmitting data and one for receiving data.'

entries.title: UART RX FIFO buffering and overflow flagging
entries.summary: While receiving, the UART EP must shift received data into a fifo-rx-buffer of length uart_rx_fifo_size, which is emptied by read requests; buffer overflow must be flagged in the UART EP status register.
entries.citation: p.110, §13.7.8.1: 'the UART EP shifts the received data into a fifo-rx-buffer that has a length of uart_rx_fifo_size... Overflow is flagged in the UART EP status register.'

entries.title: UART write request triggers transmission
entries.summary: A write request to the UART EP must result in transmission of the request's data to the externally connected device.
entries.citation: p.110, §13.7.8.1: 'A write request leads to a transmission of data to an external connected device.'

entries.title: UART read request trigger conditions and fragmentation sizing
entries.summary: A read request must be started once the fifo-rx-buffer holds as many bytes as requested (read_size), or when uart_timeout expires, or — if read_size exceeds uart_rx_fifo_size — once the fifo is full, in which case the response is fragmented; to support fragmentation correctly it is essential that uart_rx_fifo_size be chosen slightly larger than the maximum byte_msg_payload that fits in a single AVTPDU, since IEEE1722 only fragments when the payload cannot fit in one AVTPDU.
entries.citation: p.110, §13.7.8.1: 'A read request will be started as soon as the fifo-rx-buffer is filled... or when the uart_timeout has expired or in case the read_size is larger than the uart_rx_fifo_size... it is essential that the uart_rx_fifo_size is chosen such that it is slightly bigger than the maximum byte_msg_payload...'

entries.title: UART read request with payload rejected as UNKNOWN_CMD
entries.summary: A read request that carries a byte_msg_payload must be rejected by the UART EP with error code UNKNOWN_CMD.
entries.citation: p.110, §13.7.8.1: 'A read request having a byte_msg_payload will be rejected with error code = UNKNOWN_CMD.'

entries.title: UART compound wait request match against RX FIFO, limited to uart_rx_fifo_size
entries.summary: A compound wait request on the UART EP must yield a response only when the expected data matches the data currently in the fifo-rx-buffer; the amount of comparable data is therefore bounded by uart_rx_fifo_size. Cross-references §13.5.1 'Usage of evt-field in compound wait requests'.
entries.citation: p.110, §13.7.8.1: 'A compound wait request leads to a response, when the expected data matches the data in the fifo-rx-buffer, thus the amount of data to be compared is limited to uart_rx_fifo_size. See also 13.5.1 Usage of evt-field in compound wait requests.'

entries.title: UART functional configuration register map
entries.summary: Table 51 defines the UART EP functional configuration registers: uart_ep_len(0x0000,8b,R), Reserved(0x0001,8b,R, reads 0x00), pwmi_ep_enable&clr(0x0002,8b,R/W), pwmi_ep_options(0x0003,8b,R/W*), uart_ep_status(0x0004,16b,R/W), uart_baud_rate(0x0006,16b,R/W, kbit/s), uart_nr_bits(0x0008,8b,R/W), uart_parity_enable(0x0009.0,1b,R/W), uart_parity_pol(0x0009.1,1b,R/W), uart_rts_enable(0x0009.2,1b,R/W), uart_cts_enable(0x0009.3,1b,R/W), uart_half_duplex(0x0009.4,1b,R/W), uart_stop_bits(0x000A,8b,R/W, half-bit multiples; RC5 change per TI_103), uart_timeout(0x000B,8b,R/W, receiver timeout in bit times from last stop bit), uart_trail(0x000C,8b,R/W). NOTE: parameters at 0x0002/0x0003 are named 'pwmi_ep_enable&clr'/'pwmi_ep_options' rather than a uart_-prefixed name — an apparent copy/paste naming inconsistency from the PWM(I) EP section worth flagging against implementation field names.

entries.title: UART R/W parameters runtime-changeable
entries.summary: All parameters of R/W type in the UART functional configuration (Table 51) may be changed at runtime.
entries.citation: p.111, §13.7.8.2: 'All parameters of R/W-type can be changed at runtime.'

entries.title: UART request format diagram
entries.summary: Figure 31 illustrates the UART EP request byte_msg_payload format (payload plus padding if needed plus CRC if applicable) via a worked example of a 19-byte payload.
entries.citation: p.112, Figure 31 – 'uart request format'

entries.title: Client-side bit padding for non-octet uart_nr_bits
entries.summary: When uart_nr_bits is not an integer multiple of 8, the RC Client should/might need to append up to 'uart_nr_bits - 1' bits to the request payload so that it fits into an integer multiple of octets.
entries.citation: p.112, §13.7.8.3: 'In case uart_nr_bits is not a multiple integer of 8, then the RC Client might need to append up to \"uart_nr_bits - 1\" bits to create a payload in requests that fits into an integer multiple of octects.'

entries.title: UART EP appends padding bits in responses
entries.summary: Equally to the client-side padding, the UART EP must append up to 'uart_nr_bits - 1' bits in its responses when uart_nr_bits is not an integer multiple of 8, so response payloads remain octet-aligned.
entries.citation: p.112, §13.7.8.3: 'Equally the UART EP will append up to \"uart_nr_bits - 1\" bits in such cases in the responses.'

entries.title: UART EP ignores trailing non-integer-multiple bits when transmitting
entries.summary: When transmitting, if the request payload length is not an integer multiple of uart_nr_bits, the UART EP must ignore the last up to 'uart_nr_bits - 1' bits of the request payload.
entries.citation: p.112, §13.7.8.3: 'When transmitting the EP ignores the last up to \"uart_nr_bits - 1\" bits from the request payload, when the length of the payload is not an integer multiple of uart_nr_bits.'

entries.title: Optional UART HW trigger event generation
entries.summary: A UART EP may optionally generate hardware trigger events, as enumerated in Table 52, rather than being required to support triggers.
entries.citation: p.112, §13.7.8.4: 'A UART EP optionally generates HW trigger event:'

entries.title: UART trigger signal assignment table
entries.summary: Table 52 defines the mapping of UART EP output trigger signal indices to events: signal 0 = 'Transmit request finalized', signal 1 = 'Read request finalized'.
entries.citation: p.112, Table 52: 'uart trigger signals' — '0  Transmit request finalized', '1  Read request finalized'

entries.title: Analog input pin selection per ADC EP
entries.summary: Each ADC endpoint requires an analog input pin on the RC Server implementation to be selected/assigned to it.
entries.citation: p.113, "For each ADC EP an analog input pin on the RC Server implementation needs to be selected."

entries.title: Triggering ADC reads via PWM trigger event
entries.summary: Reading ADC values from an endpoint may be triggered by a PWM output trigger event, using a Trigger request that triggers on the PWM EP.
entries.citation: p.113, "Reading ADC values from an endpoint can be triggered e.g. by a PWM output trigger event by using a Trigger request, which triggers on the PWM EP."

entries.title: Cyclic ADC response generation option
entries.summary: The ADC endpoint may alternatively be configured to generate responses cyclically at a configurable cycle time, using a trigger request that triggers on the ADC EP itself finishing a measurement.
entries.citation: p.113, "The ADC endpoint can alternatively be configured to generate responses cyclically with a configurable cycle time (by using a trigger request which triggers on the ADC EP itself having finished a measurement)."

entries.title: On-demand RC Client ADC read requests
entries.summary: Independent of trigger-based configuration, the RC Client may request an ADC reading at any time.
entries.citation: p.113, "Anyhow, the RC Client may request ADCs reading at any time."

entries.title: ADC sample-taking and inter-sample spacing
entries.summary: Once a reading is requested the ADC samples; if adc_avg_intervals_per_request multiplied by adc_samples_per_avg_interval exceeds 1, further samples are taken spaced by one adc_sample_interval (expressed in multiples of adc_base_clk times adc_base_clk_divider).
entries.citation: p.113, "Once a reading is requested, then the ADC samples. If “adc_avg_intervals_per_request” multiplied by “adc_samples_per_avg_interval” is larger than 1, then further samples are taken with a timely distance of one “adc_sample_interval”..."

entries.title: ADC averaging and combine-count into response frame
entries.summary: The average is calculated for the readings acquired during each averaging interval (number of samples, implementation may fix this to 1); COMBINE_NR_VAL defines how many resulting averaging values are put into one response frame.
entries.citation: p.113, "...the average is calculated. Finally, the COMBINE_NR_VAL defines how many measurement values (i.e. averaging results) will be put in one response frame."

entries.title: Example response generation with given parameters
entries.summary: Diagram illustrating how ADC sampling, averaging-interval grouping, and COMBINE_NR_VAL combine into a generated response, for an example parameter set.
entries.citation: p.113, Figure 32 caption: "Example response generation with given parameters"

entries.title: Optional generation of ADC trigger events
entries.summary: An ADC endpoint optionally (i.e. is not required to) generates the five trigger events listed in Table 53; noted as optional since it does not apply when trigger requests are unsupported.
entries.citation: p.113, "An ADC endpoint optionally generates five trigger events:"

entries.title: ADC trigger outputs
entries.summary: Defines the 5 ADC trigger signals (0-4) and their triggering events: averaged output falling/rising below/above ADC_MIN_TRIGGER (signals 0,1), falling/rising below/above ADC_MAX_TRIGGER (signals 2,3), and ADC finished measurement interval (signal 4).
entries.citation: p.113, Table 53 caption: "adc trigger outputs"

entries.title: No trigger occurs without an active sampling request
entries.summary: The ADC only samples the input when a request is executed; consequently no trigger occurs when there is no request to sample, so continuous monitoring requires frequently repeated (e.g. repetitive-triggered or compound) requests.
entries.citation: p.113, "The ADC only samples the input, when a request is executed. Consequently, no trigger will occur when there is no request to sample."

entries.title: Compound wait request for ADC does not start sampling
entries.summary: A compound wait request targeting an ADC EP does not initiate a new sampling cycle; instead it compares its condition against the last acquired average value.
entries.citation: p.113, "A compound wait request for ADC does not start sampling. It compares against the last acquired average value."

entries.title: ADC functional configuration register map
entries.summary: Defines the ADC EP functional-configuration register layout: adc_ep_len (0x0000, 8b, R), reserved (0x0001), adc_ep_enable&clr (0x0002, 8b, R/W, common EP entry), adc_ep_options (0x0003, 8b, R/W*, common EP entry), adc_base_clk (0x0004, 16b, R), adc_ep_status (0x0006, 16b, R/W), adc_base_clk_divider (0x0008, 8b, R/W), adc_sample_interval (0x0009, 8b, R/W), adc_avg_intervals_per_request (0x000A, 8b, R/W), adc_samples_per_avg_interval (0x000B, 8b, R/W, implementation may restrict to powers of 2), adc_combine_avg_values (0x000C, 8b, R/W), adc_resolution (0x000D, 8b, R/W, <=16 bits), adc_trigger_min (0x000E, 16b, R/W), adc_trigger_max (0x0010, 16b, R/W).
entries.citation: p.114, Table 54 caption: "adc functional configuration"

entries.title: R/W ADC parameters are runtime-modifiable
entries.summary: All parameters of R/W type in the ADC functional configuration (Table 54) can be changed at runtime.
entries.citation: p.114, "All parameters of R/W-type can be changed at runtime."

entries.title: Multi-request response and transaction_num when combine > intervals
entries.summary: When adc_combine_avg_values > adc_avg_intervals_per_request, multiple requests must be executed before a response is generated; that response shall carry the transaction_num of the request that produced the first included average value.
entries.citation: p.114, "...multiple requests need to be executed, before a response will be generated. The response shall have the transaction_num of the request that generated the first average value that is included in the response."

entries.title: One response per request when combine equals intervals
entries.summary: When adc_combine_avg_values equals adc_avg_intervals_per_request, exactly one response is generated per request execution.
entries.citation: p.114, "When adc_combine_avg_values = adc_avg_intervals_per_request, then there is one response per request execution."

entries.title: Multiple responses per request when combine less than intervals
entries.summary: When adc_combine_avg_values is less than adc_avg_intervals_per_request, multiple responses are generated per single request execution.
entries.citation: p.114, "When adc_combine_avg_values < adc_avg_intervals_per_request, then there are multiple responses per request execution."

entries.title: Response timestamp semantics for combined ADC averages
entries.summary: If an ADC response includes a timestamp, it shall represent the point in time the last sample used for the first average value included in that response was captured (not the response-generation time).
entries.citation: p.115, "If the response includes a timestamp, it shall represent the point in time when the last sample that was used for the first average value that is included in the response has been captured."

entries.title: ADC request payload rule (read vs wait)
entries.summary: A standard ADC read request has no byte_msg_payload, whereas an ADC wait-request requires a byte_msg_payload.
entries.citation: p.116, "The ADC request has no byte_msg_payload, while a wait-request needs a byte_msg_payload."

entries.title: Response measurement count equals half the requested read size
entries.summary: An ADC response contains as many measurement values as requested, computed as half the read_size field of the request (each 16-bit value consuming 2 bytes of read_size).
entries.citation: p.116, "Responses contain as much measurement values as requested by half the read size of a request."

entries.title: Measured value may represent an average of multiple samples
entries.summary: Depending on ADC EP functional configuration, a single returned measured value may contain the average of multiple ADC samples rather than one raw sample.
entries.citation: p.116, "A measured value may contain the average of multiple ADC samples depending on the ADC EP functional configuration."

entries.title: LIN EP payload transmission and match-based reply
entries.summary: The LIN EP sends the bytes provided by the RC Client in byte_msg_payload on the bus in response to a pending read request. For a pending read-request it checks each received message against byte_msg_payload; if a match under the conditions given by evt[2:0] is found, a reply is sent when op = 0.
entries.citation: p.118, "It sends the bytes provided by the RC Client in the byte_msg_payload on the bus as response to a pending read request. With pending read-requests the LIN endpoint checks each received message against the byte_msg_payload and if a match under the conditions given by evt[2:0] is found a reply is sent if op = 0."

entries.title: LIN EP trigger issuance after transmission
entries.summary: The LIN EP issues a trigger when a transmission has been finalized and the configured trailing time has expired.
entries.citation: p.118, "The LIN EP issues a trigger when a transmission has been finalized, and the configured trailing time has expired."

entries.title: Cyclic LIN transmission via self-triggered repeat
entries.summary: A LIN EP configured with a repeated trigger request on its own trigger can be used to cyclically send messages on the LIN bus.
entries.citation: p.118, "A LIN EP configured with a repeated trigger request on its own trigger can be used to cyclically send messages on the Lin bus."

entries.title: CAN controller EP send/wait request handling
entries.summary: The CAN controller endpoint receives requests to either send a CAN frame (Classical CAN, CAN FD, CAN FD light or CAN XL, depending on endpoint capabilities) or wait for a specific payload to be received via CAN, possibly combined with trigger conditions or as conditional execution in a compound request.
entries.citation: p.119, "The CAN controller endpoint is receiving requests to either send a CAN (Classical CAN, CAN FD, CAN FD light or CAN XL - depending on endpoint capabilities) frame or wait for a specific payload to be received via CAN."

entries.title: CAN controller EP response creation on frame reception
entries.summary: The CAN controller creates responses upon reception of CAN frames.
entries.citation: p.119, "The CAN controller creates responses upon reception of CAN frames."

entries.title: CAN EP functional configuration scope, extensible
entries.summary: The CAN EP functional configuration comprises: bit rate settings for the arbitration phase (valid for CAN XL, CAN FD/CAN FD light and Classical CAN), bit rate settings for the CAN FD fast phase, bit rate settings for the CAN XL data phase, acceptance filter settings for CAN XL, receive ID filter settings (valid for all CAN variants), and usage of new PL (YES|NO) for CAN XL; this set may be extended depending on RC Server implementation.
entries.citation: p.119, "The functional configuration of the CAN controller comprises: ... and may be extended depending on RC Server implementation."

entries.title: CAN XL data field maximum size and segmentation
entries.summary: For CAN XL the \"CAN data\" field can be up to 2054 bytes (2048 payload bytes + 6 additional bytes), which requires segmentation, supported by the \"ms\" and \"segment_num\" fields in the request/response format.
entries.citation: p.121, "For CAN XL this can be up to 2054 bytes (2048 + 6, see below), which requires segmentation, which is supported by the fields \"ms\" and \"segment_num\"."

entries.title: Remote frames not supported
entries.summary: Sending CAN remote frames is not supported by the CAN controller EP.
entries.citation: p.122, "Sending remote frames is not supported."

entries.title: 11-bit CAN ID right-alignment in CAN ID field
entries.summary: When the CAN ID is 11 bits, it shall be right aligned within the CAN ID field of the request/response format.
entries.citation: p.122, "In case the CAN ID is 11bits, then it shall be right aligned in the CAN ID field."

entries.title: CAN data field additional XL data composition
entries.summary: For CAN XL frames (either XL variant of FrameFormat), the \"CAN data\" field includes the additional data required by ISO 11898-1 -- RRS, SDT, VCID and AF, totaling 6 bytes -- alongside the CAN XL payload.
entries.citation: p.122, "The \"CAN data\" field includes the additional data (RRS, SDT, VCID, AF (in total 6 bytes)- see ISO11898-1) needed for CAN XL frames, when the frame format is one of the two XL variants."

entries.title: ISELED optional CRC generation/check
entries.summary: The optional CRC generation defined by the ISELED standard can be enabled on the ISELED EP; when enabled the CRC is generated and attached to write messages sent to the ISELED network, and for read data the CRC is calculated and checked by the EP.
entries.citation: p.123, "The optional CRC generation as specified in the ISLED standard can be enabled. If so, the CRC will be generated and attached to the write messages to the ISELED network. For read data accordingly the CRC will be also calculated and checked."

entries.title: ISELED single trigger event on packet completion
entries.summary: The ISELED endpoint generates exactly one trigger event when transmission of a data packet on the ISELED network has completed (used for triggered/compound operation sequencing).
entries.citation: p.123, "The ISELED endpoint creates a single trigger event, when transmission of a data packet has been completed on the ISELED network."

entries.title: iseled_clk_divider nominal 2MHz target
entries.summary: The iseled_clk_divider field generates the ISELED_CLK time reference and should be set for a nominal 2MHz clock.

entries.title: ISELED receive clock source options
entries.summary: For receiving ISELED frames on the ISP_P pin, either clock synchronization via the Freq_Sync pattern or data sampling based on the clock provided on the ISP_N pin can be used; if Freq_Sync is used, ISP_N need not be connected to a physical pin.
entries.citation: p.123, "either a clock synchronization via the Freq_Sync pattern can be done or data sampling based on the clock provided on the ISP_N pin... If the Freq_Sync pattern is used it is not necessary to connect the ISP_N of the EP to a physical Pin."

entries.title: ISELED safe-operation-mode CRC handling
entries.summary: In safe-operation mode a CRC is added to ISELED request/response payloads that is not present on the underlying ISELED network wire protocol; the ISELED-specific CRC is generated by the EP and provided to the ISELED network only when configured to do so.
entries.citation: p.124, "In case of safe-operation mode a CRC will be added, that is not present on the ISELED network... The ISELED specific CRC will be generated by the EP and provided to the ISELED network if configured."

entries.title: ISELED response mandatory address/data fields
entries.summary: An ISELED response always contains the 12-bit address and 12-bit data, plus an optional 4-bit CRC.
entries.citation: p.124, "A response always contains the 12 bit address and 12 bit data plus the optional 4 bit CRC."

entries.title: MDIO EP access to integrated PHY
entries.summary: An RC Server implementation with an integrated PHY may allow access to that integrated PHY via the MDIO EP; in that case the MDIO EP has no signals mappable to physical pins.
entries.citation: p.125, "An RC Server implementation with an integrated PHY may allow access to the integrated PHY via this MDIO EP. In this case the MDIO EP does not have signals that can be mapped to physical pins."

entries.title: MDIO fixed endpoint number EP1

entries.citation: p.125, "The MDIO is EP1."

entries.title: MDIO EP has no configurable parameters
entries.summary: The MDIO EP does not expose any configurable parameters beyond the common functional-configuration entries.
